daas-irab:56-56.t: ﴿يا عِبادِيَ﴾ a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), annexed; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of «عبادي». ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين». ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي واسِعَةٌ﴾ «إن», its noun and its khabar (predicate). ﴿فَإِيَّايَ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa [fāʾ, implying an unstated condition], and «إياي» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied verb; the clause «إن أرضي» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:57-57.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ «كل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to «نفس». ﴿ذائِقَةُ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِلَيْنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to what comes after them. ﴿تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:58-58.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين». ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «آمنوا». ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾ the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam) «[Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is then called the answer to the omitted oath, i.e. the lām is the one occurring in the answer.]», and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿غُرَفاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «غرفا». ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ a delayed fāʿil. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ attached to what precedes them; the clause «نبوئنهم» is the answer to the omitted oath. ﴿نِعْمَ أَجْرُ﴾ an invariable (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise, and its fāʿil. ﴿الْعامِلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And the oath clause is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين».

daas-irab:59-59.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of «العاملين». ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to what comes after them. ﴿يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:60-60.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿كَأَيِّنْ﴾ an allusive noun for number (kināya ʿan ʿadad), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿دَابَّةٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as the tamyīz (specification) of «كأين». ﴿لا تَحْمِلُ﴾ «لا» is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿رِزْقَهَا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «دابة». ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَرْزُقُها﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «الله», the nominal clause «الله..» is the khabar of «كأين», and the clause «كأين..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِيَّاكُمْ﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the accusative pronoun in «يرزقها». ﴿وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ﴾ and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:61-61.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and «إن» is conditional. ﴿سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb with its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿مَنْ خَلَقَ﴾ «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «السموات»; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «من», and the nominal clause «من خلق...» is the second object of «سأل». ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿سَخَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الشَّمْسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ﴾ conjoined to «الشمس»; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the answer to the implied oath; ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the omitted wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the answer to the implied oath. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa [fāʾ, implying an unstated condition]; ﴿فَأَنَّى﴾ an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of the implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:62-62.t: ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَبْسُطُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الرِّزْقَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ عِبادِهِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَيَقْدِرُ﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «يبسط». ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ «إن», and the Divine Name is its noun. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ attached to the khabar «عليم». ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar.

daas-irab:63-63.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ﴾ its i'rab has been given before. ﴿مَنْ نَزَّلَ﴾ an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of «سأل». ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَأَحْيا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ also attached to the verb. ﴿مَوْتِها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. And the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; ﴿لَيَقُولُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the omitted wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the answer to the implied oath. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Divine Name, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿قُلِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ «لا» is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:64-64.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هذِهِ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْحَياةُ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ naʿt (adjective) of «الحياة». ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿لَهْوٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَعِبٌ﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «لهو». ﴿وَإِنَّ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿إِنَّ الدَّارَ﴾ «إن» and its noun. ﴿الْآخِرَةَ﴾ naʿt of «الدار». ﴿لَهِيَ﴾ the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ﴿هي الحيوان﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن», and the clause «إن..» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, non-jussive. ﴿كانُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar of «كانوا», and the clause «كانوا..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:65-65.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial, conditional, non-jussive. ﴿رَكِبُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فِي الْفُلْكِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿دَعَوُا اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil, and the Divine Name is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَهُ﴾ attached to what precedes them. ﴿الدِّينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of «مخلصين». ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿لما نجاهم﴾ «لما» is an adverb of time (ḥīniyya), and a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿إِلَى الْبَرِّ﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿إِذا﴾ of surprise (fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the answer to «لما», with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:66-66.t: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أن» and what follows them is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يشركون». ﴿بِما﴾ attached to the verb. ﴿آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ a past verb with its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «ليكفروا». ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿سوف﴾ a particle of the future. ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:67-67.t:
﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا﴾ the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation, the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by «لم», and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنَّا﴾ «أن» and its noun. ﴿جَعَلْنا حَرَماً﴾ a past verb with its fāʿil and its object. ﴿آمِناً﴾ naʿt (adjective) of «حرما»; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أن» and what follows it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَيُتَخَطَّفُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a passive imperfect verb. ﴿النَّاسُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿مِنْ حَوْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And the hamza is a particle of disapproving interrogation. ﴿أَفَبِالْباطِلِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; ﴿بالباطل﴾ attached to what comes after them. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿بِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ attached to «يكفرون», and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:68-68.t: ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿مَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أظلم». ﴿افْتَرى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Divine Name, genitive by «على»; [the two] are attached to the verb. ﴿كَذِباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من». ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ an adverb of time (ḥīniyya). ﴿جاءَهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَلَيْسَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of affirmative interrogation (taqrīr), and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the fronted khabar of «ليس». ﴿مَثْوىً﴾ the delayed noun of «ليس». ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of «مثوى»; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:69-69.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِينا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين». ﴿لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the answer to the omitted oath; ﴿نهدينهم﴾ an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿سُبُلَنا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the answer to the omitted oath, with no grammatical position, and the oath together with its answer is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين», and the clause «الذين..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, «إن» and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «مع» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar of «إن». ﴿الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:12-15.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ): resumptive speech, introduced to show another example of their misguidance.
(وقال الذين): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (للذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قال); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause (اتبعوا) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); (اتبعوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (سبيلنا) is the object; (ولنحمل): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command, and (نحمل) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; (خطاياكم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The meaning of the command will come in the section on rhetoric.
(وَما هُمْ بِحامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطاياهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which operates like laysa; (هم) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (حاملين) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position as the predicate of mā; (من خطاياهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of (شيء) and was placed before it; (من) is a redundant preposition, and (شيء) is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the object of (حاملين). The clause (إنهم لكاذبون) gives the reason for the categorical statement that they will not bear anything of their sins; inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and (كاذبون) is its predicate.
(وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ وَأَثْقالًا مَعَ أَثْقالِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and (يحملن) is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters; the wāw of the plural, dropped because two quiescent letters met, is the fāʿil; (أثقالهم) is a mafʿūl bihi; (أثقالا) is conjoined to (أثقالهم); (مع أثقالهم) is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of (أثقالا).
(وَلَيُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عَمَّا كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يسألن) is conjoined to (يحملن); (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to (يسألن); (عما) is a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to (يسألن); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila of (ما), and the clause (يفترون) is the predicate of (كانوا).
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عاماً): resumptive speech, introduced to support the obligation which Muhammad ﷺ imposed upon his followers, i.e. that it is not peculiar to the Prophet and his followers. The lām is in answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (أرسلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (نوحا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (إلى قومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أرسلنا). (فلبث): the fāʾ is a conjunction, (لبث) is a past verb, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to Noah; (فيهم) is attached to (لبث); (ألف سنة) is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), because it is a number annexed to an adverb and so took its adverbial character from it, and it too is attached to (لبث); (إلا) is a particle of exception; (خمسين) is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā); and (عاما) is a tamyīz (specification). A subtle point has been observed here which we will mention in the section on rhetoric.
(فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أخذهم الطوفان) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (ظالمون) is the khabar (predicate). Al-ṭūfān is whatever surrounds and encompasses in abundance and overwhelming force, whether a flood, the darkness of night or the like. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
حتى إذا ما يومها تصببا ... وعم طوفان الظلام الأثأبا
(Until, when its day poured down, and the flood of darkness covered the athʾab trees.)
The verse is by al-ʿAjjāj, describing a wild cow. (ما) is redundant after (إذا). (عم) is with the undotted ʿayn, and it is also transmitted with the dotted ghayn (غم); the two meanings are close. The athʾab is a kind of tree resembling the fig tree; its singular is athʾaba. Attributing "pouring down" to the day is an intellectual metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī) of the type of attribution to time, i.e. the rain poured down and its darkness covered the trees that were in it.
(فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْناها آيَةً لِلْعالَمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أنجيناه) is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (أصحاب) is conjoined to the hāʾ, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); (وجعلناها): the wāw is a conjunction, and (جعلناها) is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (آية) is a second mafʿūl bihi; and (للعالمين) is an adjective of (آية).

* Rhetoric:
1- The command used in the sense of a statement:
In His saying «ولنحمل خطاياكم» the speech is a command in the sense of a statement (khabar). That is, the underlying form of «ولنحمل خطاياكم» is: "If you follow us, we will bear your sins"; it was turned from that to what is mentioned, which runs contrary to the apparent sense, namely their commanding themselves to bear. In His saying «انهم لكاذبون» there is a fine subtle point (nukta) from which one can prove the soundness of the command coming in the sense of a statement, for some people deny this and have no proof, because Allah the Exalted followed their saying «ولنحمل خطاياكم», in the form of a command, with His saying «انهم لكاذبون», and calling someone a liar only applies to statements.
2- The subtle point of the number:
This is in His saying «فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما». Reporting it in this form prepares the excuse of Noah, peace be upon him, for invoking against his people a curse which destroyed them to the last one. For had it been said, "He remained among them nine hundred and fifty years", this expression would not have had the force of amplification that the first expression has, because the word "thousand" in the first expression is the first thing to strike the ear, and the hearer is occupied by it from hearing the rest of the speech, namely the exception; and when he returns to listening, the exception, coming after what preceded it, no longer has an impact that would remove what settled in him from the mention of "thousand". Thus the great sin of the people of Noah, peace be upon him, in persisting in disobedience despite the long period of the call, is magnified.
Al-Zamakhsharī's words on this number: "If you say: why was it not said 'nine hundred and fifty years'? I say: what Allah brought is more precise, because had it been said as you say, it would be possible to imagine this number being applied loosely to most of it, and this imagining disappears when it comes in this form; it is as if it were said 'nine hundred and fifty full years, complete in number', except that this is more concise, sweeter in wording and fuller of benefit. There is another subtle point in it, namely that the story is related to mention what Noah, peace be upon him, was tried with by his community and the long endurance he suffered, as a consolation for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to make him firm; so mentioning the head of the number, beyond which there is no greater head, was more effective and more conducive to the purpose of making the hearer feel the length of his patience."
A second subtle point in the number:
There is a second subtle point, namely that He varied the tamyīz of the two numbers, saying in the first «سنة» and in the second «عاما», so that the wording would not be heavy. Moreover, He assigned the word ʿām to the fifty to signal that when the Prophet of Allah ﷺ [Translator's note: i.e. Noah, peace be upon him; the source uses this formula here] was relieved of them, he remained in a good time; the Arabs express fertility by ʿām and drought by sana.
A third subtle point in the number:
There is a third subtle point discovered by al-Rāzī. He said: "If you say: what is the benefit of mentioning the length of his stay? I say: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to feel distressed because the unbelievers did not enter Islam, so Allah the Exalted said to him: Noah remained among his people this great number of years and only a few of his people believed, yet he was patient and did not grow weary; so you are more worthy of patience, given the shortness of your stay and the great number of your community."

* Benefits:
In His saying «ولنحمل خطاياكم»: the norm is that the lām of command and the prohibitive lā enter the verb of the absent person, active and passive, and the passive of the second person and the first person. Their entry on the active first person singular is rare; if the first person is other than singular, their entry on it is easier and lighter, as in the preceding verse and the saying of the poet:
إذا ما خرجنا من دمشق فلا نعد ... لها أبدا ما دام فيها الجراضم
(When we leave Damascus, let us never return to it as long as the glutton remains in it.)

dervis-irab:16-23.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِبْراهِيمَ إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ): resumptive speech, introducing a second story after the story of Noah and the flood. (إبراهيم) is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "Remember (adhkur)"; the adverb (إذ) is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from (إبراهيم). You may also make it conjoined speech, conjoining (إبراهيم) to (نوحا) and attaching the adverb to (أرسلنا); the meaning would then be: We sent Abraham when he reached the age at which he could address his people with words of exhortation and guidance. The clause (قال لقومه) is in the position of the genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; (لقومه) is attached to (قال).
(اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ ذلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is the object of Abraham's saying to his people. (اعبدوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is its object; (اتقوه) is conjoined to «اذكروا الله» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is «اعبدوا الله»]; (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (خير) is the khabar (predicate), and (لكم) is attached to (خير); (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and the clause (تعلمون) is its predicate. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then worship Allah and fear Him".
(إِنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً): (إنما) is a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa) one; (تعبدون) is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أوثانا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وتخلقون إفكا) is conjoined to what precedes it. (إفك) may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) or an adjective, i.e. a fabrication that is ifk, meaning possessing falsehood and vanity.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً): inna and its noun; the clause (تعبدون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; the clause (لا يملكون) is the predicate of inna; (لكم) is attached to (رزقا); (رزقا) is the object of (يملكون), because it means "what is provided", or is an interpreted maṣdar from inna [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "from an and the verb"] and the verb: that they are not able to provide for you. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar, its governor being (لا يملكون), since it carries its meaning.
(فَابْتَغُوا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الرِّزْقَ وَاعْبُدُوهُ وَاشْكُرُوا لَهُ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence); (ابتغوا) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; (عند الله) is attached to (ابتغوا); (الرزق) is the object of (ابتغوا); (اعبدوه) and (اشكروا له) are conjoined to (ابتغوا); (إليه) is attached to (ترجعون); (ترجعون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(وَإِنْ تُكَذِّبُوا فَقَدْ كَذَّبَ أُمَمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ): conjoined to what precedes and arranged in the thread of Abraham's speech, peace be upon him, to his people. (إن) is conditional; (تكذبوا) is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (فقد): the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is joined with (قد); (كذب أمم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (من قبلكم) is an adjective of (أمم). It has been said that the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "your denial does not harm me, for nations before you denied their prophets and messengers". (وما): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive, and (ما) is negative; (على الرسول) is a fronted predicate; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (البلاغ) is a postponed subject; and (المبين) is an adjective of (البلاغ).
(أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī), and the wāw conjoins to an omitted clause required by the context; (لم) is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning]; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the clause (يبدئ الله الخلق) is in the position of the accusative as the object of (يروا), because it has been suspended from operating by the interrogative. The seeing is mental (qalbiyya), meaning sound and clear knowledge, because it is like visual seeing. (ثم يعيده) is resumptive speech, or speech conjoined to (أولم يروا). The reason it cannot be conjoined to (يبدئ) is that the intent is to use what they know of the states of the beginning as proof of the return, in order to establish it; were [the return] known to them, this would be obtaining what is already obtained. It cannot be said that this is conjoining a statement (khabar) to a non-statement (inshāʾ), because the interrogative contains the meaning of disapproval and affirmation (taqrīr), and so it is equivalent to a statement. Inna and its noun; (على الله) is attached to (يسير); and (يسير) is the predicate of inna.
(قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ): the speech relates Abraham's saying to his people, or Allah's saying to Abraham. (سيروا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في الأرض) is attached to (سيروا); (فانظروا) is conjoined to (سيروا); (كيف) is a ḥāl; (بدأ الخلق) is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of (انظروا), which is suspended because of the interrogative.
(ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): (ثم) is a conjunction; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (ينشئ) is the khabar; (النشأة الآخرة) is accusative as a maṣdar with its augment letters dropped, the original being al-inshāʾa. It was also read al-nashāʾa, with lengthening; they are two dialectal forms, like raʾfa and raʾāfa. Inna and its noun; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير), and (قدير) is the predicate of inna.
(يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَرْحَمُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَإِلَيْهِ تُقْلَبُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl, or a second predicate of inna, or resumptive. (يعذب) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "huwa", referring to Allah; (من) is its object, and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila of (من); (ويرحم من يشاء) is conjoined to (يعذب من يشاء); (إليه) is attached to (تقلبون); (تقلبون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. The meaning of (تقلبون) is: you will be returned and brought back.
(وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative mā; (أنتم) is its noun, the address being to the people of the earth; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (معجزين) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the predicate of mā; (في الأرض) is a ḥāl. The object of (معجزين) is omitted because it is known, namely Allah the Exalted, i.e. you will not escape Him if you try to flee from His decree. (ولا في السماء) is conjoined to (في الأرض); if "the heaven" is taken to mean height, it is permissible, i.e. in towers and fortresses rising high, and it would be a specification after generalization. (ما) is negative; (لكم) is a fronted predicate; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; (من ولي): (من) is a redundant preposition and (ولي) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed subject; (ولا نصير) is conjoined to (من ولي).
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وَلِقائِهِ أُولئِكَ يَئِسُوا مِنْ رَحْمَتِي): (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; (بآيات الله) is attached to (كفروا); (لقائه) is conjoined to (آيات); (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ, the clause (يئسوا من رحمتي) is the predicate of (أولئك), and the clause (أولئك يئسوا) is the predicate of (الذين).
(وَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a fronted predicate; (عذاب) is a postponed subject and (أليم) an adjective of (عذاب); the clause (لهم عذاب أليم) is the predicate of (أولئك).

* Rhetoric:
1- He made "provision" indefinite in His saying (لا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقاً) and then definite in His saying «فابتغوا عند الله الرزق», because the first is confined to them and so must be meagre and little; He made it indefinite to indicate its smallness and meagreness. Since the second is sought from Allah, it must be abundant, because all of it is with Allah; so He made it definite to indicate its abundance and magnitude.
2- Pronominal reference (iḍmār) and overt mention (iẓhār):
In His saying «أولم يروا كيف يبدىء الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق ثم الله ينشىء النشأة الآخرة» there is a device which few notice, because it is extremely subtle, and a writer or poet resorts to it only for a benefit beyond the obvious, namely magnifying the importance of the matter. Do you not see that He mentioned His Name, the Exalted, explicitly in His saying «ثم الله ينشىء النشأة الآخرة», and moreover made it the mubtadaʾ, whereas the regular form would have been to say: "how Allah began creation, then [He] brings about the final creation"? So He stated His Name openly after having referred to it by a pronoun. The benefit of this is that, since the restoration was in their view one of the momentous matters, and the opening of the speech dealt with them concerning the beginning and established for them that this is from Allah, He argued against them that the restoration is a bringing-into-being like the beginning; and if Allah, whom nothing can render incapable, is the One whom the beginning does not render incapable, then the restoration must not render Him incapable either. So, to indicate and draw attention to the greatness of this matter, the restoration, He brought His Name, the Exalted, into the open and made it the mubtadaʾ. The norm in speech is overt mention followed by pronominal reference; next, for the purpose of magnification, overt mention after overt mention; and next, the most magnificent of the three, overt mention after pronominal reference, as in the verse.
By analogy with this one measures what has come in their speech, such as the saying of one of them describing an encounter with the Banū Tamīm: "When we met, the Banū Tamīm came at us galloping, and we saw among them bereaved lions racing the spear-points to the watering place, which do not turn back on their heels when their like among lions turn back; and the Banū Tamīm rallied against us all together, so we took refuge in flight and raced each other in turning our backs." It was said "and the Banū Tamīm rallied", mentioning their name explicitly, rather than "and they rallied", as was said "they came", to indicate wonder at their boldness at the charge and their steadfastness at the clash, especially since he followed that with his saying "we took refuge in flight and raced each other in turning our backs". It is as if he said: and those famous horsemen, the well-armed, formidable horsemen, rallied and charged us in a single charge, so we turned back in defeated flight.
Imam al-Rāzī pointed to this subtle point but presented it in another way, so we quote his words verbatim: "He brought the Name of Allah into the open in the first verse at the beginning, where He said 'how Allah begins creation', and used a pronoun for it at the restoration; and in this verse He used a pronoun for it at the beginning and brought it into the open at the restoration, where He said 'then Allah brings about the creation'. This is because in the first verse Allah had not been previously mentioned with a verb so that the beginning could be attributed to Him, so He said 'Allah begins' and then said 'then He restores it'; whereas in the second verse the mention of the beginning was attributed to Allah the Exalted, so that sufficed. As for openly mentioning Him at the bringing-into-being a second time, where He said 'then Allah brings about the creation', it is so that the perfection of His power, knowledge and will may settle in the mind of the hearer. He did not say 'restores it' but said 'brings about' (yunshiʾ) to draw attention to the fact that the beginning is called a nashʾa (bringing into being) just like the restoration, the difference between them being in the description, as they say: the first nashʾa and the second nashʾa."

dervis-irab:24-27.t:
* I'rab:
(فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا اقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (جواب) is its fronted predicate; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن قالوا) is an interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) which is the postponed noun of (كان), i.e. some of them said it to others, so all of them counted as sayers. (اقتلوه) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); (أو) is a conjunction and (حرقوه) is conjoined to (اقتلوه).
(فَأَنْجاهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence), i.e. "so they threw him into the fire, and Allah saved him"; (أنجاه الله) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; (من النار) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنجاه); (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted predicate; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آيات) is its postponed noun; (لقوم) is an adjective of (آيات), and the clause (يؤمنون) is an adjective of (قوم).
(وَقالَ إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): the wāw is a conjunction, and (قال) is conjoined to (أنجيناه) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «فأنجاه»]; (إنما) is a restraining particle (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa) one; (اتخذتم) is a verb and its fāʿil; (من دون الله) is in the place of the second object of (اتخذتم); (أوثانا) is the first object of (اتخذتم); (مودة) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I mean (aʿnī)"; (بينكم) is annexed to (مودة) as muḍāf ilayhi; (في الحياة الدنيا) is attached to (اتخذتم) or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
This verse has greatly occupied the grammarians because of the differences in its readings and the divergence of viewpoints about it. We have kept the i'rab brief, following the reading of Ḥafṣ, and chose the best and easiest of the analyses; in the section on benefits we will quote a drop from the ocean of what has been said about it, to sharpen the mind.
(ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَيَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً): (ثم) is a conjunction expressing delay; (يوم القيامة) is an adverb attached to (يكفر); (بعضكم) is the fāʿil; (ببعض) is also attached to (يكفر); (ويلعن بعضكم بعضا) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi.
(وَمَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ): (مأواكم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) or a fronted khabar (predicate), and (النار) is the predicate or a postponed subject; the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (لكم) is a fronted predicate; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (ناصرين) is a postponed subject, genitive (majrūr) in form.
(فَآمَنَ لَهُ لُوطٌ وَقالَ إِنِّي مُهاجِرٌ إِلى رَبِّي إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (آمن) is a past verb and (لوط) is its fāʿil; (له) is attached to (آمن); (وقال) is conjoined to (فآمن), and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Abraham. For this reason one must pause at (لوط), because His saying (إني مهاجر) is Abraham's speech; if it were joined, one might imagine that the second verb belongs to Lot, and the meaning would be corrupted. Inna and its noun; (مهاجر) is its predicate; (إلى ربي) is attached to (مهاجر), i.e. to wherever my Lord commands me, so there is a figure of speech (majāz) in the words. Inna and its noun; (هو) is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; (العزيز) is the predicate of (إني) [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause is «إنه»], or the predicate of (هو), the clause then being the predicate of (إني); and (الحكيم) is a second predicate.
(وَوَهَبْنا لَهُ إِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِ النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ): (وهبنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (له) is attached to (وهبنا); (إسحاق) is a mafʿūl bihi and (يعقوب) is conjoined to it; (جعلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (في ذريته) is in the place of the second object, and «الشجرة» is the first object [Translator's note: so in the source; it should read «النبوة» (prophethood), which is the first object]; (الكتاب) is conjoined to (النبوة).
(وَآتَيْناهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي الدُّنْيا وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): (آتيناه) is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is a conjunction [Translator's note: so in the source]; (أجره) is a second mafʿūl bihi; (في الدنيا) is a ḥāl; (وإنه): inna and its noun; (في الآخرة) is a ḥāl; the lām is the shifted lām; and (من الصالحين) is the predicate of (إنه).

* Benefits:
We have presented to you the best of the analyses in the i'rab of His saying, the Exalted, «وقال إنما اتخذتم من دون الله أوثانا مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا», and promised to quote some of what has been said about it, all of it fine speech and sound reasoning. We begin with what al-Zamakhsharī said: "It has been read in the accusative without annexation and with annexation, and likewise in the nominative. The accusative is as a cause, i.e. so that you may love one another and be brought together by your gathering to worship them and your agreement on them, just as people agree on a doctrine and it becomes the cause of their mutual love and friendship. Or it is a second object, like His saying «اتخذ إلهه هواه», i.e. you have taken the idols as the cause of affection between you, on the assumption that the muḍāf is omitted; or you have taken them as affection between you, in the sense of 'loved among you', like His saying, the Exalted: «ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم كحب الله». In the nominative there are two analyses: that it is the predicate of inna, on the basis that (ما) is a relative noun; or that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, the meaning being that the idols are affection between you, i.e. loved, or a cause of affection. From ʿĀṣim: «مودة بينكم» with (بينكم) in the fatḥa along with annexation, just as «لقد تقطع بينكم» was read with the fatḥa while it is the fāʿil. Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, read: «أوثانا انما مودة بينكم في الحياة الدنيا», i.e. you only love one another upon them, or you love them, in the life of this world."
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: "«وقال انما اتخذتم»: concerning (ما) here there are three analyses:
The first: that it is a relative noun meaning 'that which', the referring pronoun being omitted, which is the first object; (أوثانا) is a second object; and the predicate is (مودة) in the reading of those who read it in the nominative, as will come. The implied form is: 'that which you have taken as idols is affection', i.e. possessing affection, or it was made affection itself, for hyperbole. And [the predicate] is omitted in the reading of those who read (مودة) in the accusative, i.e. 'that which you have taken as idols for the sake of affection will not benefit you', or 'will be against you', as indicated by His saying «ثم يوم القيامة يكفر بعضكم ببعض».
The second: that you make (ما) restraining (kāffa) and (أوثانا) the object; the taking here is transitive to one object or to two, the second being (من دون الله). For those who read (مودة) in the nominative, it is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. 'it is affection', i.e. possessing affection, or it was made affection itself for hyperbole; the clause is then an adjective of (أوثانا) or resumptive. For those who read it in the accusative, it is an object for the sake of which (mafʿūl lahu), or by implying 'I mean'.
The third: that you make (ما) maṣdariyya; then one may assume a muḍāf from the first, i.e. 'the cause of your taking idols is affection', for those who read (مودة) in the nominative; or one may not assume it, but make the taking itself the affection, for hyperbole. In the reading of those who read the accusative, the predicate is omitted, as in the first analysis. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read (مودة) in the nominative without tanwīn and (بينكم) in the genitive; Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr read (مودة) in the accusative with tanwīn and (بينكم) in the accusative; Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ read (مودة) in the accusative without tanwīn and (بينكم) in the genitive. The nominative has been covered, and the accusative too, with two analyses; a third analysis is permissible, namely to make it a second object, by hyperbole, through the extended use of the adverb. Those who read it in the accusative read it according to its original state. It is transmitted from ʿĀṣim that he read (مودة) in the nominative without tanwīn and (بينكم) in the accusative; this was explained as the annexation of (مودة) to the adverb, which was made indeclinable only because it is annexed to something non-declinable, like the reading «لقد تقطع بينكم» with the fatḥa, if we make (بينكم) the fāʿil."
In the book of Abū al-Baqāʾ his words are: "His saying, the Exalted, «انما اتخذتم»: concerning (ما) there are three analyses. The first: it means 'that which', the referring pronoun being omitted, i.e. 'you have taken it'; (أوثانا) is a second object or a ḥāl; and (مودة) is the predicate in the reading of those who read the nominative, the implied form being 'possessing affection'. The second: it is restraining, (أوثانا) is the object, and (مودة) in the accusative is an object for the sake of which, and in the nominative by implying a subject, the clause being an adjective (naʿt) of the idols; the accusative may also be as an adjective, i.e. 'possessing affection'. The third analysis: that (ما) is maṣdariyya and (مودة) in the nominative is the predicate; in this analysis there is no omission in the predicate but in the noun of inna, the implied form being 'the cause of your taking is affection'. (مودة) is read with annexation in the nominative and the accusative, with (بينكم) in the genitive, and with tanwīn on (مودة) in both cases, with (بين) in the accusative. Concerning what (في الحياة الدنيا) is attached to, there are seven analyses: (first) that it is attached to (اتخذتم) if you make (ما) restraining, but not in the other two analyses, lest it lead to separating the relative noun from what is in the ṣila by the predicate; (second) that it is attached to (مودة) itself if you do not make (بين) its adjective, because a maṣdar, when qualified, does not govern; (third) that you attach it to (بينكم) itself, because its meaning is 'your gathering' or 'your union'; (fourth) that you make it a second adjective of (مودة) if you give it tanwīn and make (بينكم) an adjective; (fifth) that you attach it to (مودة) and make (بينكم) an adverb of place, so that (مودة) governs both; (sixth) that you make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in (بينكم) if you make it an adjective of (مودة); and (seventh) that you make it a ḥāl from (بينكم), since it is made definite by annexation. Some of them allowed (في) to be attached to (مودة) even if (بينكم) is an adjective, because adverbs are treated with latitude, unlike the direct object."

dervis-irab:28-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نادِيكُمُ): al-nādī, al-nadwa and al-muntadā are the assembly of the people by day, or the assembly as long as they are gathered in it. Its plural is andiya; do not say nawādin. The author of al-Munjid erred in giving its plural as nawādin. "The nādī does not hold them (mā yandūhum)" means the assembly does not have room for them because of their great number. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "An assembly is not called a nādī except as long as its people are in it; when they rise and leave it, it no longer remains a nādī."

* I'rab:
(وَلُوطاً إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الْفاحِشَةَ ما سَبَقَكُمْ بِها مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): conjoined to (إبراهيم), or accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "Remember (udhkur)". The adverb is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from (لوطا); the clause (قال) is in the position of the genitive, the adverb being annexed to it; (لقومه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قال); the clause (إنكم لتأتون) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); inna and its noun, the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause (تأتون) is its predicate, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); (الفاحشة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause (ما سبقكم) is resumptive, introduced to affirm its foulness and the ugliness of the one who commits it; Abū Ḥayyān preferred that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), as if He said: "Do you commit the indecency, innovating it, not preceded in it?" (ما) is negative; (سبقكم) is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi; (بها) is attached to (سبقكم); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (أحد) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position as the fāʿil of (سبقكم); (من العالمين) is an adjective of (أحد).
(أَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ السَّبِيلَ وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نادِيكُمُ الْمُنْكَرَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); (إنكم): inna and its noun; the shifted lām; the clause (تأتون) is the predicate of inna; (الرجال) is a mafʿūl bihi; (وتقطعون السبيل) is conjoined to (تأتون الرجال). It was said that they used to commit the indecency with travellers who passed by them, and when they did that, people stopped passing by them, so they cut off the road for this reason. (تأتون) is also conjoined; (في ناديكم) is attached to (تأتون); and (المنكر) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا ائْتِنا بِعَذابِ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; (جواب) is the fronted predicate of (كان); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن) and what is in its scope form the postponed noun of (كان); the clause (ائتنا) is the maqūl al-qawl; (ائتنا) is an imperative verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (بعذاب الله) is attached to (ائتنا); (إن) is conditional; (كنت) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and (من الصادقين) its predicate. The apodosis of (إن) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then bring us the punishment of Allah".
(قالَ رَبِّ انْصُرْنِي عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): (رب) is the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the vocative particle is omitted; (انصرني) is a verb of supplication, the fāʿil latent, the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; (على القوم) is attached to (انصرني), and (المفسدين) is an adjective of (القوم).

dervis-irab:31-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ذَرْعاً): al-dharʿ is capacity and strength. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Ḍāqa bil-amri dharʿan: he was unable to bear it; a person's dharʿ is the capacity he can reach." Al-Zamakhsharī's words: "The Arabs made narrowness of the forearm (al-dhirāʿ) and of the dharʿ an expression for lack of capacity, just as they said 'wide of forearm in such a thing' when one is able to bear it. Its origin is that when a man's forearm is long, he reaches what the short-armed cannot reach, so this was coined as a metaphor for incapacity and ability." In al-Asās and al-Lisān there are remarkable figurative uses of this word, for it is said: ḍāqa bil-amri dharʿan and dhirāʿan when he cannot bear it; abṭarta nāqataka dharʿahā: you burdened your she-camel with what she cannot bear; iqṣid bi-dharʿika wa-rbaʿ ʿalā ẓalʿika: be gentle with yourself; mā laka ʿalayya dhirāʿ, i.e. any power; I went around in the madhāriʿ of the valley, which are its outskirts and sides; adhraʿa fī kalāmihi, he is yudhriʿu fīhi idhrāʿan, which is speaking at length; so-and-so is my dharīʿa (means) to you, and I have tadharraʿtu (sought access) by him to him, i.e. used him as a means; I asked him about his affair and he dharraʿa (disclosed) something of it to me; dharaʿtu for so-and-so with the governor: I interceded for him, and I am his dharīʿ (intercessor) with him; a dharīʿ death befell them: swift and widespread, that is when they could no longer bury one another; it became straight like the dhirāʿ al-ʿāmil, which is the upper part of the spear-shaft; it is for you from me on the rope of the forearm (ḥabl al-dhirāʿ), i.e. present and near; and I placed your affair on your forearm, i.e. do as you wish.
Further, the dhirāʿ of a man is from the tip of the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, and also the forearm (sāʿid); it is feminine in both senses and may be masculine. The dhirāʿ as a measure is between fifty and seventy centimetres long.
(رِجْزاً): al-rijz and al-rijs: punishment, from their saying irtajaza and irtajasa when one is agitated, because of the anxiety and agitation that befall the one punished.

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا إِبْراهِيمَ بِالْبُشْرى قالُوا إِنَّا مُهْلِكُوا أَهْلِ هذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ): the wāw conjoins to an omitted clause required by the context, i.e. Allah answered Lot's prayer and sent angels to destroy them and commanded them to give Abraham the glad tidings of good offspring, so they came first to Abraham. (لما) is temporal, meaning "when" (ḥīniyya), or a linking particle; (جاءت رسلنا إبراهيم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (بالبشرى) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاءت); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause (إنا) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); inna and its noun; (مهلكو) is its predicate; (أهل) and (هذه) are both muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (القرية) is a badal (substitute) from (هذه). It is Sadhūm or Sadūm (Sodom), and its detailed mention has preceded, so refresh your memory of it.
(إِنَّ أَهْلَها كانُوا ظالِمِينَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the destruction; inna and its noun; the clause (كانوا) is its predicate, and (ظالمين) is the predicate of (كانوا).
(قالَ: إِنَّ فِيها لُوطاً قالُوا نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ فِيها): (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (فيها) is its fronted predicate and (لوطا) its postponed noun. The meaning of this statement will come in the section on rhetoric. (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أعلم) the khabar (predicate); (بمن) is attached to (أعلم), and (فيها) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من).
(لَنُنَجِّيَنَّهُ وَأَهْلَهُ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَهُ كانَتْ مِنَ الْغابِرِينَ): the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (ننجينه) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "naḥnu"; (أهله) is conjoined to the hāʾ, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); (إلا) is a particle of exception; (امرأته) is the excepted (mustathnā), and this has preceded. The clause (كانت) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (كانت) is a defective past verb, its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "hiya", and (من الغابرين) is its predicate, i.e. those who remain in the punishment.
(وَلَمَّا أَنْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا لُوطاً سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً): (أن) is redundant (zāʾida) after (لما), conveying a delay together with sequence in two adjacent times with no gap between them; its like has preceded in Yūsuf. The clause (سيء بهم) has no grammatical position; (سيء) is a passive past verb; (بهم) is attached to (سيء); and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. distress and grief came to him because of them, in the manner of the poet's saying:
يغضي حياء ويغضى من مهابته ... فما يكلّم إلا حين يبتسم
(He lowers his eyes out of modesty, and eyes are lowered out of awe of him, so he is not spoken to except when he smiles.)
A detailed account of this will come in the section on benefits. (وضاق بهم) is conjoined to (سيء); (ذرعا) is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil, i.e. his capacity was straitened by them. It is also possible that the nāʾib fāʿil is a pronoun referring to Lot.
(وَقالُوا لا تَخَفْ وَلا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ كانَتْ مِنَ الْغابِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إنا): inna and its noun; (منجوك) is its predicate, and the kāf is in the position of the genitive by annexation. Accordingly, (أهلك) is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We will save your family". The i'rab of what follows has preceded.
(إِنَّا مُنْزِلُونَ عَلى أَهْلِ هذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ رِجْزاً مِنَ السَّماءِ بِما كانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ): inna and its noun; (منزلون) is its predicate; (على أهل هذه القرية) is attached to (منزلون); (رجزا) is the object of (منزلون), because it is an active participle; (من السماء) is an adjective of (رجز); (بما): the bāʾ is causal and (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. because of their transgression; kāna and its noun, and the clause (يفسقون) is its predicate.
(وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْنا مِنْها آيَةً بَيِّنَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (تركنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (منها) is attached to (تركنا), or is its second object, with (آية) its first object and (بينة) an adjective. This is because the grammarians differ about «ترك»: some make it transitive to one object, and some make it mean "to make (ṣayyara)", hence to two objects, which is the choice of Ibn Mālik, who cited:
وربيته حتى إذا ما تركته ... أخا القوم واستغنى عن المسح ساربه
(I raised him until, when I made him a man among men and his moustache no longer needed wiping...)
(لقوم) is attached to (بينة), and the clause (يعقلون) is an adjective of (قوم).

* Rhetoric:
The device of allusion (ishāra):
In His saying «ان فيها لوطا» there is the device of allusion, which has been mentioned many times in this book. What is intended is not to inform them that Lot is in the town; rather, it is an argument on his behalf, because they mentioned that its people would be destroyed because of their persistence in wrongdoing, so he objected to them that in it there is one whose record is free of sin, who has not committed a sin nor perpetrated a crime, nor shared with his people the error and relapse in which they persist. In all this there is also an allusion to the fact that it is the duty of the believing person to grieve for his brother, to hasten to repel injustice from him and to roll up his sleeves to defend him. This is among the eloquent and hidden forms of allusion.

* Benefits:
The deputy agent (nāʾib al-fāʿil):
After the fāʿil is omitted, one of four things takes its place:
1- The mafʿūl bihi, as in «وغيض الماء وقضي الأمر».
2- The noun made genitive by a preposition, as in «ولما سقط في أيديهم», on condition that the preposition is not causal; so one does not say "wuqifa laka" nor "min ajlika". In its i'rab one says that it is genitive in form by the preposition and nominative in position as the nāʾib fāʿil. However, if it is feminine, its verb is not made feminine but remains masculine; so one does not say "dhahabat bi-Fāṭima" but "dhuhiba bi-Fāṭima".
3- The specified, fully declinable (mutaṣarrif) adverb, as in "a whole day was walked" and "Ramaḍān was fasted". By a mutaṣarrif adverb is meant one to which predication can soundly be made, like day, night, age and month; the non-mutaṣarrif is one to which predication cannot soundly be made, like ḥaythu and ʿinda. By "specified" is meant that it is informative, not vague, and specified by a description, as in "an instructive session was sat", or by annexation, as in "I stayed awake the Night of Power", or by being a proper name, as in "Ramaḍān was fasted". So vague adverbs such as time, moment and place, when not annexed, do not take the place of the fāʿil.
4- The specified, fully declinable maṣdar, as in «فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة»: (نفخة) is the nāʾib fāʿil, being a declinable maṣdar to which predication can soundly be made, and specified because it is qualified; "sīra sayrun" is not allowed because it conveys no benefit. The [pronoun of the] declinable, specified maṣdar may take the place of the fāʿil, and of this is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
يغضي حياء ويغضى من مهابته ... فما يكلّم إلا حين يبتسم
(He lowers his eyes out of modesty, and eyes are lowered out of awe of him, so he is not spoken to except when he smiles.)
The meaning is then: the known lowering of the eyes is done, namely the lowering of reverence, out of awe of him; so the nāʾib fāʿil is the pronoun of the lowering understood from (يغضي). It is not permissible for (من مهابته) to be in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil, because the preposition here is causal, so it is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). Among its examples also is the saying of Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd al-Bakrī:
فيا لك من ذي حاجة حيل دونها ... وما كل ما يهوى امرؤ هو نائله
(What a man of need you are, whose need has been barred! Not everything a man desires does he attain.)
The meaning is then: the known barring was done; it is not sound for it to be the adverb, because it is not mutaṣarrif.

dervis-irab:36-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلا تَعْثَوْا): and do not cause corruption. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "ʿathā yaʿthū and ʿathiya yaʿthā, of the pattern of qāla and taʿiba: he caused corruption, so he is ʿāth." In al-Qāmūs: "ʿathā, like ramā, saʿā and raḍiya, ʿuthiyyan, ʿithiyyan and ʿathayānan; and ʿathā yaʿthū ʿuthuwwan: he caused corruption."
(الرَّجْفَةُ): the violent earthquake. In al-Asās: "The earth rajafat (quaked): «فأخذتهم الرجفة», «يوم ترجف الأرض والجبال»; the tree rajafa and the wind arjafathu; the camel rajafa under the saddle, and the mounts under their saddles are rawājif and rujjaf; an old man came to us whose bones were trembling. Among the figurative uses: they went out yastarjifūna the earth in rescue; the two sides of the east and the west trembled with them; arjafū in the city with such-and-such when they spread news of it in order to cause agitation among people, without it having been confirmed [Translator's note: the source reads «يصيح»; probably «يصحّ» (to be confirmed) is meant] with them; this is among the arājīf (rumours) of the misguided; and irjāf is the prelude to the event. And you say: when fears occur, rumours multiply."
(حاصِباً): a raging (ʿāṣifa) wind containing pebbles (ḥaṣbāʾ). In al-Mukhtār: "The wind ʿaṣafat: it became violent; its pattern is ḍaraba."

* I'rab:
(وَإِلى مَدْيَنَ أَخاهُمْ شُعَيْباً فَقالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَارْجُوا الْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إلى مدين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb conjoined to (أرسلنا) in the story of Noah, i.e. "and We sent to Madyan Shuʿayb"; (أخاهم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (شعيبا) is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "huwa"; (يا) is a vocative particle and (قوم) is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person; the rule of the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person has passed. (اعبدوا الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (ارجوا) is conjoined to (اعبدوا); (اليوم) is a mafʿūl bihi and (الآخر) is an adjective of (اليوم).
(وَلا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تعثوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في الأرض) is attached to (تعثوا); and (مفسدين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (كذبوه) is a past verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (فأخذتهم): the fāʾ is a conjunction, (أخذتهم) is a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and (الرجفة) is a postponed fāʿil; (فأصبحوا) is conjoined to (فأخذتهم), the wāw being the noun of aṣbaḥa; (في دارهم) is attached to (جاثمين), and (جاثمين) is the predicate of (أصبحوا).
(وَعاداً وَثَمُودَ وَقَدْ تَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ مِنْ مَساكِنِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (عادا) is the object of an omitted verb conjoined to what precedes, i.e. "and We destroyed ʿĀd"; (ثمود) is conjoined to (عادا), [read] both as a triptote and as a diptote; the wāw is a conjunction; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (تبين) is a past verb, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "their destruction"; some estimated it as "clear signs from which you take admonition and on which you reflect". (من مساكنهم) is attached to (تبين), i.e. from the direction of their dwellings when you pass by them.
(وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أَعْمالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَكانُوا مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (زين) is a past verb; (لهم) is attached to (زين); (الشيطان) is the fāʿil and (أعمالهم) a mafʿūl bihi; (فصدهم) is conjoined to (زين); (عن السبيل) is attached to (صدهم); the wāw is circumstantial; (كانوا) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw its noun and (مستبصرين) its predicate, i.e. while they were capable of reflection and insight, but they deafened their ears and blinded their eyes to the truth and to seeing its signs.
(وَقارُونَ وَفِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ وَلَقَدْ جاءَهُمْ مُوسى بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما كانُوا سابِقِينَ): (قارون) is conjoined to (عاد), and (فرعون) and (هامان) are conjoined to it. Qārūn was mentioned first because of his kinship with Moses; i.e. We destroyed them all. The wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); (قد) is a particle of affirmation; (جاءهم) is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (موسى) is the fāʿil; (بالبينات) is attached to (جاءهم); (فاستكبروا) is conjoined to (جاءهم); (في الأرض) is attached to (استكبروا); the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (كانوا): kāna and its noun, and (سابقين) is its predicate, i.e. they persisted in their transgression, but they could not escape, and Our punishment overtook them.
(فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنا بِذَنْبِهِ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِ حاصِباً): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ of eloquence), i.e. if you wish to know their fate, We seized each of them for his sin. (كلا) is a fronted object of (أخذنا), and (أخذنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (فمنهم): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (منهم) is a fronted predicate and (من) a postponed subject, which is an indefinite noun qualified (nakira mawṣūfa); (أرسلنا) is an adjective; (عليه) is attached to (أرسلنا); and (حاصبا) is the object of (أرسلنا).
(وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَخَذَتْهُ الصَّيْحَةُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ خَسَفْنا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَغْرَقْنا): the wāw is a conjunction; (منهم) is a fronted predicate and (من) a postponed subject; the clause (أخذته الصيحة) is an adjective. (ومنهم من خسفنا به الأرض) is conjoined to the one before it, and likewise (ومنهم من أغرقنا).
(وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلكِنْ كانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (كان الله): kāna and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), and (يظلمهم) is accusative by (أن) necessarily implied after the lām of denial; the wāw is circumstantial; (لكن) is lightened and inoperative; (كانوا): kāna and its noun; (أنفسهم) is a fronted object; and the clause (يظلمون) is the predicate of (كانوا).

dervis-irab:41-44.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعَنْكَبُوتِ): a well-known small creature which spins threads from its saliva and catches its food with that web. The plural is ʿanākib and ʿankabūtāt. Al-ʿankab is the male, plural ʿanākib and ʿanākīb; al-ʿankaba, al-ʿankabāh and al-ʿaknabāh are the female, plural ʿanākib and ʿanākīb. The scholars of morphology said: "Al-ʿankabūt is well known; its nūn is radical, and the wāw and tāʾ are augments, as evidenced by their saying in the plural ʿanākib and in the diminutive ʿunaykib. It is masculine and feminine, and this is regular in generic nouns." Ibn Yaʿīsh said in Sharḥ al-Mufaṣṣal: "Of this is [the pattern] faʿlalūt: they said ʿankabūt and takhrabūt, and it does not occur as an adjective. Al-ʿankabūt is well known, a small creature which spins for itself houses of flimsy threads; al-takhrabūt is the sprightly she-camel. The wāw and tāʾ at their end are augments, added at the end of the quadriliteral just as they are added at the end of the triliteral, as in malakūt and rahabūt." The discussion of the simile relating to the spider's house will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِياءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتاً وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ): the state of the one who took idols as protectors, worshipped them and relied on them, hoping for their benefit and intercession, is like the state of the spider, as will come in the section on rhetoric. (مثل) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila (relative clause), being a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من دون الله) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أولياء) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كمثل) is the khabar (predicate), and its like has preceded; (العنكبوت) is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause (اتخذت بيتا) is a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the source does not parse «وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت» here.]
(لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ): (لو) is conditional; kāna and its noun, and the clause (يعلمون) is its predicate. The apodosis (jawāb) of (لو) is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have worshipped them".
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): the clause gives the reason for what precedes it. Inna and its noun; the clause (يعلم) is its predicate; (ما) is a relative noun, the object of (يعلم); the clause (يدعون) is the ṣila, and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. He knows those whom they call upon and knows their states; what is meant by the reason is to emphasize the parable He struck. (من دونه) is a ḥāl; (من شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يدعون). (ما) may also be negative, with (من شيء) the object of (يدعون), (من) being redundant (zāʾida) because it is preceded by negation, and the clause (ما يدعون) is in the position of the accusative as the object of (يعلم). (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (العزيز) a first predicate and (الحكيم) a second predicate. Some said: "(ما) is interrogative, negative or relative, and (من) is partitive or redundant for emphasis; and it was said that this clause is on the implication of the saying, i.e. say to the unbelievers: Allah knows whatever thing they call upon besides Him."
(وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثالُ نَضْرِبُها لِلنَّاسِ وَما يَعْقِلُها إِلَّا الْعالِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (تلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (الأمثال) is a badal (substitute); the clause (نضربها للناس) is the khabar. (الأمثال) may also be the predicate, and the clause (نضربها) a ḥāl or a second predicate. The wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (يعقلها) is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (العالمون) is the fāʿil of (يعقلها). The discussion of parables will come in the section on rhetoric.
(خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): resumptive speech, beginning the consolation of the believers after despair of the unbelievers' faith had taken hold of them. (خلق الله السموات) is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (بالحق) is a ḥāl, the bāʾ being of accompaniment (mulābasa); (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is the fronted predicate of inna; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آية) is the postponed noun of inna; and (للمؤمنين) is an adjective of (آية).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت» there is the device of representation (tamthīl), select examples of which have preceded. Some make it a kind of metaphor (istiʿāra) and illustrate it with the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي ... بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتّل
(Your eyes did not shed tears except that you might strike with your two arrows into the tenths of a heart already slain.)
He likened her eyes to two arrows of the maysir game, namely al-muʿallā, which has seven shares, and al-raqīb, which has three shares; so all the tenths of his heart went to the two arrows to which he likened her eyes. He likened his heart to the tenths of the slaughtered camel, so the aspects of metaphor and representation were complete for him. In the verse, He likened what they took as a support and reliance in their religion and took as protector besides Allah to that which is proverbial among people for flimsiness and weakness of strength, namely the spider's web; i.e. just as it is true that the flimsiest of houses is the spider's house, so it is true that their religion is the weakest and flimsiest of religions.
Among the fine examples of representation is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa, whose poetry they used to call "the shelled pistachio":
أيها المنكح الثريا سهيلا ... عمّرك الله كيف يلتقيان
هي شامية إذا ما استهلت ... وسهيل إذا استقل يماني
(O you who marry al-Thurayyā to Suhayl, by Allah, how can they ever meet? She is northern when she appears, and Suhayl, when it rises, is southern.)
He means al-Thurayyā, daughter of ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Umayya al-Aṣghar, who was the utmost in beauty and perfection, and Suhayl ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who was the extreme of ugliness and homeliness. He drew a parallel between them and their two namesakes [the Pleiades and Canopus], and meant only the distance and disparity between them specifically, because the southern Suhayl is ugly [Translator's note: so in the source], not homely.
Upon this also came the saying of al-Mutanabbī, from an ode in which he mentions the revolt of Shabīb the Khārijite and his rebellion against Kāfūr:
برغم شبيب فارق السيف كفه ... وكانا على العلات يصطحبان
كأن رقاب الناس قالت لسيفه ... رفيقك قيسي وأنت يماني
(Against Shabīb's will the sword parted from his palm, though in all conditions the two had been companions; as if the necks of the people said to his sword: your companion is a Qaysī, and you are Yamānī.)
Shabīb the Khārijite, who revolted against Kāfūr al-Ikhshīdī, marched on Damascus, besieged it and was killed during its siege, was from Qays, and there were constant enmities and wars between Qays and Yemen; the reports of that are well known. The sword is called Yamānī as an attribution to Yemen. Al-Mutanabbī's meaning is that when Shabīb was killed and the sword parted from his palm, it was as if people said to his sword: you are Yamānī and your companion is Qaysī, and for this reason the sword shunned him and left him.
Representation in the view of ʿAbd al-Qāhir:
There is another reason which ʿAbd al-Qāhir mentions, explaining by it the splendour of representation, and which he regards as encompassing the bounds of the subject. That is that conceiving the resemblance of a thing in something not of its genus and form opens another door of elegance and subtlety and one of the ways of perception whose place in the mind is not hidden. If you survey similes, you find that the greater the distance between the two things, the more wondrous they are to souls and the more souls delight in them; and representation is the most particular of things in this respect.
ʿAbd al-Qāhir said: "Do you doubt that it works like magic in combining disparate things, until it shortens the distance between east and west? It shows you the represented meanings as likenesses in visible persons, makes the dumb speak to you, gives you eloquence from the inarticulate, shows you life in the inanimate, shows you the joining of very opposites, and makes a thing near and far at once." We will be content with this much now, on condition that we return to this discussion in another place in this book.

dervis-irab:45-49.t:
* I'rab:
(اتْلُ ما أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ): resumptive speech, introduced to urge the recitation of the Book, reflection on its contents and acting on its rulings, and the establishment of the prescribed prayer performed in congregation, to unify the community and purify the soul of the stains of impurities. (اتل) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "anta", i.e. O Muhammad; the address is to him so as to include every individual of his community. (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (أوحي) is the ṣila (relative clause); (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوحي); (من الكتاب) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (أقم) is an imperative verb conjoined to (اتل), its fāʿil also latent, its implied form being "anta"; and (الصلاة) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(إِنَّ الصَّلاةَ تَنْهى عَنِ الْفَحْشاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تَصْنَعُونَ): the clause gives the reason for the command to establish the prayer. Inna and its noun; the clause (تنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر) is its predicate; the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); (ذكر الله) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أكبر) the khabar (predicate); (والله): the wāw is a conjunction, (الله) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يعلم) is the khabar, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "huwa"; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause (تصنعون) is the ṣila.
(وَلا تُجادِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ): resumptive speech, introduced to begin explaining the guidance of the People of the Book and how to argue with them. (لا) is prohibitive; (تجادلوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أهل الكتاب) is a mafʿūl bihi; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بالتي) is attached to (تجادلوا), and the noun qualified by the relative is omitted, i.e. "with the argument which"; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ and (أحسن) the khabar, the clause being the ṣila of (التي). (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (الذين) is an exception from the same genus. In the meaning there are two analyses, which Abū al-Baqāʾ presented. He said: "The first: except those of them who do wrong, so do not argue with them in the best way but with harshness, because they are harsh with you; it is then excepted from 'that which is best', not from the arguing. The second: do not argue with them at all, but let the sword judge them because of their excessive obstinacy."
(وَقُولُوا آمَنَّا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا وَأُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَإِلهُنا وَإِلهُكُمْ واحِدٌ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (قولوا) is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause (آمنا) is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying); (بالذي) is attached to (آمنا); the clause (أنزل) is the ṣila; (إلينا) is attached to (أنزل); (وأنزل إليكم) is conjoined to (أنزل إلينا), so there is an omission of the nominal relative in the speech, i.e. "and that which was sent down to you". (وإلهنا): the wāw is a conjunction, (إلهنا) is a mubtadaʾ, (إلهكم) is conjoined to (إلهنا), and (واحد) is the khabar; (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ; (له) is attached to (مسلمون), and (مسلمون) is the predicate of (نحن). In this saying there is the utmost sincere counsel, fairness and persuasion.
(وَكَذلِكَ أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ): the kāf is the adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "like that sending down We sent down"; (أنزلنا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (إليك) is attached to (أنزلنا); (الكتاب) is a mafʿūl bihi.
(فَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ): the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿiyya); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آتيناهم) is the ṣila, being a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; (الكتاب) is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يؤمنون به) is the predicate of (الذين).
(وَمِنْ هؤُلاءِ مَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَما يَجْحَدُ بِآياتِنا إِلَّا الْكافِرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (من هؤلاء) is a fronted predicate; (من) is a postponed subject; the clause (يؤمن به) is the ṣila. This is of the type of informing about unseen things, which is one of the distinguishing features of the Noble Qur'an. The wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negative; (يجحد) is a nominative imperfect verb; (بآياتنا) is attached to it; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الكافرون) is the fāʿil of (يجحد).
