﴿فإذا ركبوا في الفلك دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا: an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of condition; ركبوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause ﴿ركبوا﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; في الفلك: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ركبوا; the clause ﴿دعوا الله﴾: has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; مخلصين: a ḥāl (circumstantial); له: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مخلصين; الدين: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of مخلصين, because ﴿مخلصين﴾ is an active participle; and the clause ﴿فإذا ركبوا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون﴾: the fāʾ: a conjunction; لما: an adverb (ẓarf) meaning "when", containing the sense of condition; نجاهم: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إلى البر: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نجاهم; إذا: of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and together with what it governs it is a clause with no grammatical position, because it is the response of لما; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause يشركون: the khabar (predicate) of «هم».

muyesser-irab:66-66.t: ﴿ليكفروا بما آتيناهم وليتمتعوا فسوف يعلمون﴾: the lām: the lām of causation (taʿlīl) or the lām of consequence (ʿāqiba); يكفروا: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن concealed after the lām, the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb being genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يشركون﴾; or the lām is the lām of command, and the imperfect after it is jussive (majzūm); the wāw of the plural: fāʿil (agent); بما: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿يكفروا﴾; the clause ﴿آتيناهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; ليتمتعوا: conjoined to ليكفروا, so it is like it; the fāʾ: the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an omitted clause); سوف: a particle of futurity; and يعلمون: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:67-67.t:
﴿أولم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم﴾: the hamza: for disapproving, affirmative interrogation (istifhām inkārī taqrīrī); the wāw: conjoining to something omitted, i.e. "We have made them secure, settled in Makka, and have they not known that?"; لم: a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; يروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the wāw: fāʿil (agent); أنا: أن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), ﴿نا﴾ its noun, and the clause جعلنا its khabar (predicate); the first object of جعلنا is omitted, i.e. "We made their town Makka"; حرمًا: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أن and what follows it: fills the place of the two objects of يروا; آمنًا: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿حرما﴾; the wāw: circumstantial (ḥāliyya); يتخطف: an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); الناس: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and من حولهم: a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أفبالباطل يؤمنون وبنعمة الله يكفرون﴾: the hamza: for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); the fāʾ: conjoining to something omitted; بالباطل: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يؤمنون﴾; and ﴿بنعمة الله يكفرون﴾: conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:68-68.t:
﴿ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا أو كذب بالحق لما جاءه﴾: the wāw is resumptive; من: an interrogative noun containing the sense of negation, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); أظلم: khabar (predicate); ممن: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أظلم; the clause ﴿افترى على الله﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ﴿كذبا﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb افترى, i.e. "he fabricated and contrived a lie", or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "he fabricated for the sake of lying", or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "he fabricated while lying", and it is an emphasising ḥāl. The clause ﴿ومن أظلم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; أو: a conjunction; كذب: conjoined to افترى; بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذب; لما: temporal ("when"); and جاءه: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أليس في جهنم مثوى للكافرين﴾: the hamza is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī); ليس: a defective past verb; في جهنم: the fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس; مثوى: its postponed noun; and للكافرين: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of مثوى.

muyesser-irab:69-69.t: ﴿والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا وإن الله لمع المحسنين﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿جاهدوا﴾: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; the object of جاهدوا is omitted; فينا: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاهدوا; the lām: occurring in the response to an implied oath; the clause ﴿لنهدينهم﴾: the khabar (predicate) of الذين; سبلنا: a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or accusative by removal of the preposition; the clause ﴿والذين جاهدوا...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إن الله: إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters) and the Name of Majesty its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and مع المحسنين: an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t: ﴿أحسب الناس أن يتركوا أن يقولوا آمنا وهم لا يفتنون﴾: ﴿أحسب﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and (حسب) is a past verb; ﴿الناس﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); أن and what lies within its scope stand in place of the two objects of حسب; the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from ﴿أن يقولوا﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by an implied (muqaddar) lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يتركوا﴾; the clause ﴿آمنا﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿لا يفتنون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾; the clause is circumstantial.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿ولقد فتنا الذين من قبلهم فليعلمن الله الذين صدقوا وليعلمن الكاذبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is in answer to an implied oath; (قد) is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿فتنا﴾: verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿الذين﴾ is its object; ﴿من قبلهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. The fāʾ is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; ﴿يعلمن﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the Majestic Name is the fāʿil; ﴿الذين﴾ is its object, and the clause ﴿صدقوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿وليعلمن الكاذبين﴾ is conjoined to what preceded.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿أم حسب الذين يعملون السيئات أن يسبقونا﴾: (أم): disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning "بل" (rather) plus the interrogative hamza, the implied form being "بل أحسب ..."; the interrogation is for disapproval (inkār); ﴿حسب﴾ is a past verb; ﴿الذين﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿يعملون السيئات﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. أن and what lies within its scope stand in place of the two objects of حسب.
﴿ساء ما يحكمون﴾: the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿ساء﴾ is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the fāʿil is necessarily latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿هو﴾. ﴿ما﴾: a described indefinite (nakira mawṣūfa) in the position of accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of the fāʿil of ﴿ساء﴾, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted. The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿ما﴾, the implied form being "ساء حكمًا يحكمونه" (evil is a judgement that they make).
Or ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun meaning "الذي" (that which), in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of ﴿ساء﴾, and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "حكمهم" (their judgement). The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya. The clause ﴿يحكمون﴾ is the ṣila of maṣdariyya ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. The interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from ﴿ما﴾ and what it entered upon is the one specified for blame, the implied form being "ساء حكمًا حكمهم" (evil as a judgement is their judgement).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿من كان يرجو لقاء الله فإن أجل الله لآت وهو السميع العليم﴾: ﴿مَن﴾ is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿كان﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the noun of كان is latent (mustatir), referring to من; the clause ﴿يرجو﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of كان; ﴿لقاء﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ); ﴿إن أجل﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (أجل) its noun, the Majestic Name muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿آت﴾ is the khabar of إن; the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ, and ﴿السميع العليم﴾ are two khabars of ﴿هو﴾; the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of من.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿ومن جاهد فإنما يجاهد لنفسه إن الله لغني عن العالمين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿مَن﴾ is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿جاهد﴾ is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb); ﴿إنما﴾: a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿يجاهد﴾ is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; ﴿لنفسه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يجاهد﴾; (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Majestic Name its noun, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿غني﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿عن العالمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿غني﴾; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لنكفرن عنهم سيئاتهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (الذين): mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿وعملوا الصالحات﴾ is conjoined to آمنوا; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; (نكفرن): an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿الذين﴾; ﴿عنهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نكفرن﴾; (سيئاتهم): mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولنجزينهم أحسن الذي كانوا يعملون﴾: ﴿ولنجزينهم﴾ is conjoined to ﴿لنكفرن﴾; ﴿أحسن﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿الذي﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿يعملون﴾ is the khabar of كانوا.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ووصينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); ﴿وصينا﴾: verb and fāʿil (agent); (الإنسان): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿بوالديه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿وصينا﴾; ﴿حسنا﴾ is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "إيصاء ذا حسن" (an enjoining possessing goodness); the clause ﴿ووصينا الإنسان...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (جاهداك): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the alif is the fāʿil, and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; (لتشرك): the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and (تشرك) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of causation, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿جاهداك﴾; ﴿بي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿تشرك﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿تشرك﴾; (ليس): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; ﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ليس﴾, placed first; ﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ﴿عِلْم﴾; ﴿عِلْم﴾ is the postponed noun of ليس; the clause ﴿ليس لك به علم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the apodosis is a clause; (لا) is prohibitive; ﴿تطعهما﴾ is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, while the mīm and the alif are two letters indicating the dual; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of إن.
﴿إلي مرجعكم فأنبئكم بما كنتم تعملون﴾: ﴿إليَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ﴿مرجعكم﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿أنبئكم﴾ is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "أنا", and the kāf is an indeclinable pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; ﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أنبئكم﴾; the clause ﴿كنتم﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿تعملون﴾ is the khabar of كنتم.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿والذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لندخلنهم في الصالحين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; (الذين): mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿وعملوا الصالحات﴾ is conjoined to آمنوا; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; (ندخلن): an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن"; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿في الصالحين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ندخلنهم﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ومن الناس من يقول آمنا بالله﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); ﴿من الناس﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿مَن﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ﴿يقول ...﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿آمنا﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); ﴿بالله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿آمنا﴾; the clause ﴿ومن الناس...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.
﴿فإذا أوذي في الله جعل فتنة الناس كعذاب الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إذا): an adverb (ẓarf) of the future containing the sense of condition; ﴿في الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أوذي﴾; the clause ﴿أوذي﴾ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; the clause ﴿جعل﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا; ﴿فتنة﴾ is the first object of جعل, and (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿كعذاب﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the second object; ﴿عذاب﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the Majestic Name is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ولئن جاء نصر من ربك ليقولن إنا كنا معكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) is a jussive-governing conditional particle; ﴿جاء﴾ is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (نصر): fāʿil (agent); ﴿من ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿جاء﴾, or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نصر﴾. ﴿ليقولن﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; (يقولن): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw of the plural, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿إنا كنا معكم﴾ is the object of the saying; (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿نا﴾ its noun, and the clause ﴿كنا﴾ its khabar; ﴿معكم﴾: an adverb attached to an omitted khabar of ﴿كان﴾.
﴿أوليس الله بأعلم بما في صدور العالمين﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the wāw conjoins to something omitted that the context requires; ﴿ليس﴾ is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the Majestic Name its noun; the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) particle; (أعلم): genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar of ليس; ﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿أعلم﴾; ﴿في صدور العالمين﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. (العالمين): muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t: ﴿وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا وليعلمن المنافقين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; ﴿يعلمن﴾ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the Majestic Name is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿الذين﴾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿وليعلمن المنافقين﴾ is conjoined to ﴿وليعلمن الله الذين آمنوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿وقال الذين كفروا للذين آمنوا اتبعوا سبيلنا ولنحمل خطاياكم﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); ﴿قال الذين﴾: verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿للذين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾; the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿اتبعوا﴾ is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); (اتبعوا): verb and fāʿil; ﴿سبيلنا﴾: object; the clause ﴿وقال الذين كفروا...﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position; ﴿لنحمل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of command (lām al-amr), and (نحمل) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; (خطاياكم): mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وما هم بحاملين من خطاياهم من شيء إنهم لكاذبون﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, which operates like ليس; ﴿هم﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بحاملين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿حاملين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative (manṣūb) in position, genitive (majrūr) in form by the bāʾ; ﴿من خطاياهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of شيء and was placed before it; (من) is a connective particle, and (شيء) is genitive in form, accusative in position, because it is the object of حاملين; the clause ﴿إنهم لكاذبون﴾ is causal (taʿlīl); (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), ﴿هم﴾ its noun, the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿كاذبون﴾ its khabar.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿وليحملن أثقالهم وأثقالا مع أثقالهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath; ﴿يحملن﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters, and the wāw of the plural, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿أثقالهم﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأثقالًا﴾ is conjoined to أثقالهم; ﴿مع﴾ is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أثقالًا﴾; ﴿أثقالهم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وليسألن يوم القيامة عما كانوا يفترون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿يسألن﴾ is conjoined to يحملن; ﴿يوم القيامة﴾: an adverb attached to ﴿يسألن﴾, and (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿عما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun likewise attached to ﴿يسألن﴾; the clause ﴿كانوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, a clause with no grammatical position. (كان) is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, the wāw of the plural is its noun, and the clause ﴿يفترون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of كان.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه فلبث فيهم ألف سنة إلا خمسين عاما﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أرسلنا﴾: verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿نوحًا﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿إلى قومه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾. The clause ﴿ولقد أرسلنا نوحا﴾ is resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿فلبث﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (لبث) a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); ﴿فيهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿لبث﴾; ﴿ألف سنة﴾ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and it is likewise attached to ﴿لبث﴾; (إلا): a particle of exception (istithnāʾ); ﴿خمسين﴾ is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā); ﴿عامًا﴾ is a tamyīz (specification).
﴿فأخذهم الطوفان وهم ظالمون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿أخذهم الطوفان﴾: a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and a postponed fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿هم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ظالمون) the khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة وجعلناها آية للعالمين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; ﴿أنجيناه﴾: verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وأصحاب﴾ is conjoined to the hāʾ, or a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); (السفينة): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وجعلناها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿جعلناها﴾ is verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; ﴿آية﴾ is the second mafʿūl bihi; ﴿للعالمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وإبراهيم إذ قال لقومه﴾: the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (إبراهيم) is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of ﴿إبراهيم﴾; ﴿قال﴾ is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the clause (قال لقومه) is in the position of genitive by annexation; ﴿لقومه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾.
﴿اعبدوا الله واتقوه ذلكم خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون﴾: the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of Abraham to his people; ﴿اعبدوا﴾ is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the Majestic Name is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿واتقوه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿اذكروا الله﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in this ayah is ﴿اعبدوا الله﴾]; ﴿ذلكم﴾ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), ﴿خير﴾ khabar (predicate), and ﴿لكم﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿خير﴾; (إن) is conditional; ﴿كنتم﴾ is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿تعلمون﴾ its khabar; the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "فاعبدوا الله واتقوه" (then worship Allah and fear Him).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا﴾: (إنما): a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); ﴿تعبدون﴾: an imperfect verb and fāʿil (agent); ﴿من دون الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the Majestic Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿أوثانًا﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وتخلقون إفكًا﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it.
﴿إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا﴾: (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (الذين) its noun, and the clause (تعبدون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿من دون الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause ﴿لا يملكون﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of إن; ﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿رزقًا﴾; (رزقًا): the mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يملكون﴾, because it has the meaning of "that which is provided" (al-marzūq).
﴿فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له إليه ترجعون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted clause); (ابتغوا): imperative verb and fāʿil; ﴿عند الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ابتغوا﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, "جار ومجرور", though عند is an adverb (ẓarf)]; ﴿الرزق﴾ is the object of ابتغوا; ﴿واعبدوه واشكروا له﴾ is conjoined to ابتغوا; ﴿إليه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿ترجعون﴾; (ترجعون): an imperfect verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿وإن تكذبوا فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم﴾: conjoined to what preceded; (إن) is conditional; (تكذبوا): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿فقد﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb), because it is joined with قد, and (قد) is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿كذب أمم﴾: verb and fāʿil; ﴿من قبلكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمم; and it has been said: the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "فلا يضرني تكذيبكم، فقد كذب أمم من قبلكم أنبياءهم ورسلهم" (your denial does not harm me, for nations before you denied their prophets and messengers).
﴿وما على الرسول إلا البلاغ المبين﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); (ما) is negating; ﴿على الرسول﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿البلاغ﴾ is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿المبين﴾ is a naʿt of ﴿بلاغ﴾; the clause ﴿وما على الرسول...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, a clause with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t: ﴿أولم يروا كيف يبدئ الله الخلق ثم يعيده إن ذلك على الله يسير﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; the wāw conjoins to something omitted that the context requires; ﴿لم﴾ is a particle of negation, jussive and conversion (to the past); ﴿كيف﴾ is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause ﴿يبدئ الله الخلق﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of يروا; ﴿ثم يعيده﴾ is resumptive speech with no grammatical position; (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), (ذلك) its noun; ﴿على الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسير﴾; (يسير): the khabar (predicate) of إن.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿قل سيروا في الأرض فانظروا كيف بدأ الخلق﴾: (سيروا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سيروا﴾; ﴿فانظروا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿سيروا﴾; ﴿كيف﴾ is an indeclinable interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿بدأ الخلق﴾: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil, and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of انظروا, which is suspended (muʿallaq) because of the interrogative.
﴿ثم الله ينشئ النشأة الآخرة إن الله على كل شيء قدير﴾: (ثم): a conjunction; (الله): mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (ينشئ): khabar (predicate); ﴿النشأة الآخرة﴾ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun, i.e. absolute object); (إن) is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), the Majestic Name its noun; ﴿على كل شيء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ﴿قدير﴾; (قدير): the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء وإليه تقلبون﴾: the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or a second khabar (predicate) of إن, or resumptive, with no grammatical position; (يعذب): an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah; (من): a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿ويرحم من يشاء﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعذب من يشاء﴾; (إليه): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقلبون﴾; ﴿تقلبون﴾ is an imperfect verb in the passive (mabnī li-mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وما أنتم بمعجزين في الأرض ولا في السماء وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negating mā, which operates like ليس; ﴿أنتم﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بمعجزين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿معجزين﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative (manṣūb) in position, genitive (majrūr) in form by the bāʾ; ﴿في الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the object of معجزين is omitted since it is known, i.e. Allah the Exalted; ﴿ولا في السماء﴾ is conjoined to ﴿في الأرض﴾; ﴿ما﴾ is negating; ﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; ﴿من دون الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the Majestic Name is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿من ولي﴾: (من) is a connective particle, and (ولي) is genitive in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿ولا نصير﴾ is conjoined to من ولي.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t: The first (أَنْ) is in the position of the accusative through (حسب); it together with its ṣila (relative clause) stands in place of the two objects, according to the view of Sībawayh. The second (أَنْ) is in the position of the accusative in one of two ways: in the sense of "because they say", "for their saying" and "on condition that they say"; the other way is that the implied form be "do they think that they [will be left alone] to say".

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: It is said: its meaning is "He makes their affair manifest", because the one who makes the matter manifest is the one who knows it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنا): Abū Isḥāq said: that is, the way we follow in our religion. (وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطاياكُمْ): he said: it is a command with the import of condition and requital, that is: if you follow our way, we will carry your sins, as the poet said: [wāfir] 329-
فقلت ادعي وأدعو إنّ أندى ... لصوت أن ينادي داعيان
(So I said: call, and I will call; the farthest-reaching voice is when two callers call out.)
That is: if you call, I will call. «ولِيحمل» with kasra on the lām is also possible; that is the original form, except that the kasra was dropped for lightness. The real meaning — and Allah knows best — is: follow our way, and we will stand for you in the place of those commanded to carry your sins, if you have sins, as you say: قلّدني وزر هذا ("lay the burden of this on me").

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقالَهُمْ): plural of ثِقل ("burden"); الثَّقل [Translator's note: so in the source, probably الوَقْر, "deafness"] is in the ear; and sometimes one enters upon the other.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
There is an ellipsis in the discourse; the meaning is: We sent Noah to his people to call them to faith, and he called them to it for a thousand years less fifty years, and made the proofs manifest, but they denied him. This ellipsis is indicated by (فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ), and this story has been mentioned in more than one place in the Qurʾān. (أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ) is accusative as an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi). (إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ) is accusative as an exception from an affirmative statement. According to Sībawayh it is like the object, because it is excepted from [the statement] like an object; according to al-Farrāʾ [it is accusative] through إنّ, because in his view [إلّا] is «إن» into which «لا» has entered, so in his view the accusative is through إنّ and the nominative, when it is nominative, is through لا. As for Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], in his view it is a pure object, as though, in his view, you said: "I excepted Zayd." Abū Jaʿfar said: I saw Abū Isḥāq holding that this view of Abū al-ʿAbbās is wrong, and in his view nothing is permissible in it except what Sībawayh said. We dictate the words of Abū Isḥāq on the exception that he mentioned concerning the verse verbatim, because of their excellence and because he explained in them things belonging to this chapter. Abū Isḥāq said: «Exception in the speech of the Arabs is the confirmation and exact determination of number», because you may mention a whole while what is actually the case is most of it. When you want to confirm its completeness, you say "all of them", and when you want to confirm its deficiency, you bring in the exception. You say: جاءني إخوتك ("your brothers came to me"), meaning that all of them came to you; and it is possible that you mean that most of them came to you. When you say: جاءني إخوتك كلّهم ("your brothers all came to me"), you have confirmed the sense of the whole and made it known that none of them stayed behind. And you say: جاءني إخوتك إلّا زيدا ("your brothers came to me except Zayd"), confirming that the group is short of Zayd. Likewise the round numbers are likened to groups. You say: عندي عشرة ("I have ten"); it may be short and it may be complete. When you say: عندي عشرة إلّا نصفا ("I have ten less a half") or "ten complete", you have made known its exact amount. Likewise when you say: لبث ألفا إلّا خمسين ("he remained a thousand less fifty"), it is like your saying "ten less a half", because you have used the exception for what belongs more to ten than to nine, since the half has entered the domain of the tenth. Were you to say "ten less one" or "less two", it would be permissible but there is ugliness in it, because "nine" and "eight" express that number; yet it is permissible by way of emphasis, [meaning] that this nine neither increases nor decreases, because in your saying "ten less one" you have given the exact number. The preferred practice in exception with numbers that are the round units of fractions and whole numbers is to except [a small part]. As for excepting half of a thing, it is very ugly; the Arabs do not speak so. When you say "I have ten less five", the five is not excepted from the ten, because it is not close to it. Exception is only used in the way deficiency is expressed: you say عندي درهم ينقص قيراطا ("I have a dirham short of a qīrāṭ"); but if you said "I have a dirham short of five dāniqs" or "short of half of it", more appropriate for that would be "I have half a dirham", because the name "dirham" does not apply to half a dirham, whereas the name "brothers" applies to some of your brothers.
(فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفانُ): derived from طاف يطوف ("to go around"); it is a noun applied to whatever surrounds things, whether drowning, killing or anything else. (وَهُمْ ظالِمُونَ): mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:15-16.t: (فَأَنْجَيْناهُ وَأَصْحابَ السَّفِينَةِ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the hāʾ. Al-Kisāʾī said: (وَإِبْراهِيمَ) is accusative through (أنجينا), meaning that it is conjoined to the hāʾ; and he allowed it to be conjoined to (نوح), the meaning being "and We sent Abraham". A third view is that it is accusative in the sense of "and remember Abraham".

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: (إِنَّما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً): accusative through (تعبدون), and «ما» is the restraining mā (kāffa). It may not be redundant (ṣila) [here meaning a zāʾida that lets إنّ operate], because إنّ does not fall on a verb. If after «ما» there is a noun, and you say إنما زيد جالس ("Zayd is only sitting"), then ما is also kāffa, though some grammarians allowed it to be redundant, so that you say: إنما زيدا جالس. Outside the Qurʾān it is permissible to put أوثان in the nominative, by making «ما» a noun as the subject of إنّ with «تعبدون» as its ṣila — the hāʾ [the returning pronoun] being dropped because of the length of the noun — and making أوثانٌ the khabar of إنّ. As for (وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً), it is accusative through the verb and nothing else.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: (وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ): Abū Isḥāq mentioned two views on it. One is that the meaning is: "you cannot escape [Him] on earth, nor can the people of heaven"; the other is: "nor even if you were in heaven". Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, who said: the meaning is: "you cannot escape [Him] on earth, nor can whoever is in heaven", taking مَن not as a relative but as indefinite, with "in heaven" as its naʿt (adjective); then the naʿt was put in place of what it qualifies. Abū Isḥāq said: this is wrong, because when من is indefinite it must have a naʿt, so [the naʿt] has become like a ṣila for it; and it is not permissible to drop the relative and keep the ṣila, nor likewise its naʿt when it is like a ṣila. Rather, people were addressed in terms they know, and in their view whoever is in heaven is farther to reach; so the meaning is: you cannot escape [Him] on earth, and even if you were in heaven you would not escape. Its like is (أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ وَلَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُرُوجٍ مُشَيَّدَةٍ) [al-Nisāʾ: 78]. [Translator's note: in the source the refutation is attributed to Abū Isḥāq even though the narration came from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd via ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān; translated as written.]

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ): the khabar of كان, and its noun is (إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا). It is also possible to put «جواب» in the nominative, making it the noun of كان, with the khabar (أَنْ قالُوا).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (وَقالَ إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثاناً مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): this [i.e. مودّةُ بينِكم, nominative and annexed] is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī. Abū Isḥāq said: مودّةٌ بينَكم has also been read. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read (مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ) [i.e. مودّةً بينَكم] [Translator's note: the source prints مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ throughout; the readings are distinguished here according to the explanation that follows and the known transmission: the Medinans, ʿĀṣim (in Shuʿba's transmission) and Ibn ʿĀmir: مودّةً بينَكم; Ḥamza (and Ḥafṣ): مودّةَ بينِكم], and Ḥamza read مودّةَ بينِكم. The first reading, with مودّة in the nominative, has three explanations, two of which Abū Isḥāq mentioned. One is that it is nominative as the khabar of إنّ, with ما meaning الذي; the implied form is: "that which you have taken as idols besides Allah is [the bond of] affection among you". The other explanation is that it rests on an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "it is affection", or "that is affection among you", the meaning being: your intimacy and your gathering are affection among you. The third explanation, which he did not mention, is that «مودّة» is nominative as mubtadaʾ and (فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) is its khabar. As for the annexation of مودّة to بينكم, he made بينكم a noun, not an adverb; the grammarians say: he made it an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). Sībawayh reported: [rajaz] يا سارق الليلة أهل الدار ("O you who rob the people of the house tonight"). It may not be annexed to while it is an adverb, for a reason this is not the place to mention. The second reading is on the basis that he made بينكم an adverb and so put it in the accusative. The third reading is on the basis that he put مودّة in the accusative because he made it a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), as you say: جئتك ابتغاء العلم ("I came to you seeking knowledge") and قصدت فلانا مودّة له ("I went to so-and-so out of affection for him").

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (وَآتَيْناهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي الدُّنْيا): two objects. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have discussed it and explained its meaning. (وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): «في الآخرة» is not included in the ṣila [Translator's note: the source has «الضلة», read as الصلة]; it is only an explanation (tabyīn). We have discussed it elsewhere at greater length than this.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (وَلُوطاً إِذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ): al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "and We saved Lot", or "and We sent Lot". He said: and this explanation is dearer to me.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
The reading of the Kufans is (أَإِنَّكُمْ) in the first and the second, as a question; likewise the reading of Abū ʿAmr, except that he lightens [the hamza]. Nāfiʿ read إنّكم without a question in the first, and with a question in the second. This reading follows the written text (al-sawād), and it is by way of charging them (ilzām), not a question. Likewise Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said about the poet's words: [khafīf]
330-
ثمّ قالوا: تحبّها قلت: بهرا
(Then they said: "You love her?" I said: "Exceedingly!")
The first reading, according to Abū ʿUbayd, is far-fetched because it combines two questions. Abū Jaʿfar said: the matter is not so, because this is a question after a question, and two questions in a case like this are not objectionable; he likened it to what does not resemble it among the things he mentioned in this sūra.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
(فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ): there are two views on it. One is that صدقوا is derived from الصدق ("truthfulness") and الكاذبين from الكذب, which is the opposite of truthfulness; the meaning then is: Allah will surely make manifest those who were truthful, who said "we are believers" and believed likewise, and those who lied when they believed otherwise; and [those who] were truthful in their saying "we will be steadfast and stand firm with the Prophet ﷺ in battle"; and He will know those who lied. The other view is that صدقوا is derived from الصَّدْق, which is "hard, firm", and الكاذبين from كذب in the sense of "he fled in defeat"; the meaning then is: Allah will surely know those who stood firm in battle and those who fled, as the poet said: [basīṭ] 328-
ليث بعثر يصطاد الرّجال إذا ... ما الّليث كذّب عن أقرانه صدقا
(A lion of ʿAththar that hunts men; when a lion flinches from its peers, it stands firm.)
And فليعلمنّ was put in place of ليبيّننّ ("He will surely make manifest") figuratively.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ): conjoined to the kāf by interpretation; it is not permissible to conjoin it to its position without interpretation, lest an overt genitive noun be conjoined to a pronoun. (إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ): an exception from an affirmative statement.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (وَعاداً وَثَمُودَ): al-Kisāʾī said: some of them said: it refers back to the beginning of the sūra: (وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ ... وَعاداً وَثَمُودَ). He said: and dearer to me is that it be on (فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ), "and it seized ʿĀd and Thamūd". Abū Isḥāq claimed that the implied form is: "and We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd". (وَكانُوا مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ): there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: they were clear-sighted in their misguidance. The other view is: they were clear-sighted, that is, they had known truth from falsehood through the manifestation of the proofs. This view is more likely — and Allah knows best — because one only says "so-and-so is clear-sighted (mustabṣir)" when he knows the thing as it truly is; and whoever disbelieves without knowing the thing as it truly is, his case cannot escape one of two aspects: either he is obstinate, or he has abandoned the reasoning and seeking to know the truth that were obligatory on him; and on either of these he is punished.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: (وَقارُونَ وَفِرْعَوْنَ وَهامانَ): al-Kisāʾī said: if you wish, it is on ʿĀd, with what that involves; and if you wish, it is on (فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ) [al-Naml: 24] [Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase also occurs in al-ʿAnkabūt: 38], "and he turned Qārūn, Pharaoh and Hāmān away".

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ): Abū Isḥāq construed «ما» in two ways. One is that it is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "evil is it as a thing that they judge". The other construal is that «ما» is in the position of the nominative, in the sense of "evil is the thing: their judgement". Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān construed it in two other ways besides those: one is that «ما» together with يحكمون is as a single thing, as you say: أعجبني ما صنعت ("what you did pleased me"), that is, "your deed". He said: but if you said ساء صنيعك ("evil is your deed") it would not be permissible. The other construal is that «ما» has no grammatical position and has taken the place of the noun for ساء; likewise with نعم and بئس. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: I prefer to give «ما» a position in every case where I am able to, such as the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: (فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ) [Āl ʿImrān: 159], likewise (فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ) [al-Nisāʾ: 155], and likewise (أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ) [al-Qaṣaṣ: 28]: «ما» is in the position of the genitive in all of these, and what follows it is a follower (tābiʿ) of it; and likewise (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً) [al-Baqara: 26]: «ما» is in the position of the accusative and بعوضة is a follower of it.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: (فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنا بِذَنْبِهِ): al-Kisāʾī said: «فكلّا» is accusative through (أخذنا).

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِياءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative by interpretation, because it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, in the position of the accusative as an adverbial. العنكبوت ("the spider") is feminine; al-Farrāʾ reported it as masculine and recited: [wāfir] 331-
على هطّالهم منهم بيوت ... كأنّ العنكبوت هو ابتناها
(On their Haṭṭāl [a mountain] they have houses, as though the spider himself had built them.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: there are several plurals of العنكبوت: one says عناكب, عناكيب, عكاب, عكب and أعكب; and it has been reported that one says عنكب. (وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He struck a parable for the weakness and frailty of their gods, and likened them to the house of the spider.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: He said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يَدْعُونَ), that is, whatever thing you worship besides Him. Abū Jaʿfar said: «من» here is partitive; if it were redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, the meaning would be reversed.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: The doctrine of Abū al-ʿĀliya is that the meaning is "[the recitation] of what is recited in the prayer"; the implied form on this view is "the recitation of the prayer", like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]. Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned something else besides this. (وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ): the doctrine of al-Ḍaḥḥāk is that the meaning is: remembering Allah at what is forbidden, so that it is abandoned, is the most exalted remembrance. It is also said: the meaning is: Allah's remembrance [of you] is a greater forbidding of indecency and wrongdoing, that is, great; أكبر may mean كبير ("great").

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: (وَلا تُجادِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ): a badal (substitute) for (أهل); it may also be an exception.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made this a proof of his prophethood, because he did not write and did not mix with the People of the Book, and there were no People of the Book in Mecca; yet he brought them the reports of the prophets and the nations, and suspicion and doubt were removed by these things.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: (بَلْ هُوَ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ): that is, rather the Book is. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is بل هي آيات بينات, in the sense of "rather the verses of the Qurʾān are clear signs". He said: its like is (هذا بَصائِرُ) [al-Jāthiya: 20]; had it been هذه, it would have been permissible; and its parallel is (هذا رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّي) [al-Kahf: 89] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Kahf: 98].

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (مَنْ كانَ يَرْجُوا لِقاءَ اللَّهِ): the exegetes hold that the meaning is: whoever fears death, let him do righteous deeds, for it will inevitably come to him. «من» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); «كان» is in the position of the khabar (predicate) and in the position of the jussive as the condition; «يرجو» is in the position of the khabar of كان; and the requital (apodosis) is (فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ).

nahhas-irab:50-51.t: (وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): their demanding this was out of obstinacy and mockery, because enough signs had appeared, and this was something without end; so he was commanded to say to them: (إِنَّمَا الْآياتُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ), that is, He brings of them what contains benefit. (وَإِنَّما أَنَا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ): it is said: its meaning is that he makes clear to them what is obligatory on them. He made the first point clear by His saying: (أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ): «أنّا» is in the position of the nominative through (يكفي).

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: This [وكأيّن] is «أيّ» into which the kāf of comparison has entered, so that it has acquired the meaning of «كم». The implied form according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them both, is "like the number". Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān explained this, saying: [it is] "what thing among things"; so the meaning according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is "like a large number of things". He said: and that is why al-Kisāʾī said: the origin of «كم» is كما; so when you say كم مالك? the meaning is: like what number is your wealth? He said: similar to that in vagueness is له كذا وكذا درهما ("he has such-and-such dirhams"), that is, he has like the number mentioned or pointed to; then their use of it increased until they said له كذا even when nothing had preceded and nothing was pointed to. When you say له عندي كذا درهما, according to the Kufans he is owed eleven dirhams; when you say له عندي كذا وكذا درهما, he is owed twenty-one dirhams; when you say له عندي كذا درهمٍ, it is a hundred; and when you say كذا دراهم, it is three. According to the Basrans the genitive is not permissible in any way, and it is in their view vague, applying to few and many. Abū ʿUbayda claimed that الحيوان, الحياة and الحيّ are one [in meaning]. Others say: الحيّ is a plural on the pattern fuʿūl, like عصيّ.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: (وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا): the lām of purpose (lām kay); it may also be the lām of command, because the original vowel of the lām of command is kasra, except that it is a command carrying the sense of threat. Whoever read وَلْيتمتّعوا with sukūn on the lām did not make it the lām of purpose, because the lām of purpose may not be made vowelless.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: (وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the lām of emphasis. The lām entered upon مع on one of two bases: one is that it is a noun, and the lām of emphasis enters only upon nouns; the other is that it is a particle, and [the lām] enters upon it because it carries the meaning of settledness (istiqrār), as you say: إنّ زيدا لفي الدار ("Zayd is indeed in the house"). «مع», when it is vowelless [مَعْ], is a particle and nothing else; when it has fatḥa, it may be a noun or a particle. Mostly it is a particle that came for a meaning, except that it was given fatḥa because of what occurs in it that is not in its sisters.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً): Abū Isḥāq said: it is like "We enjoined on man, regarding his parents, what is good". He said: إحسانا has been transmitted [as a reading], and the meaning is: We enjoined on man, regarding his parents, that he treat them with excellence (iḥsānan).

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤـمۤ. أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوۤاْ أَن يَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾.
This is a question carrying the sense of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīr and tawbīkh): that is, do people think that they will be satisfied with merely saying "we believe", and not be tested so that the reality of their faith and their patience, their truthfulness and their lying, may be known and become manifest from them, and they be recompensed for it? As for the unseen, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, already knew it of them.
Then He said ﴿أَن يَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا﴾, that is: on the basis that they say, and because they say, and by their saying, "we believe".
﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: that is, they will not be put to trial.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
That is, We tried them.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ أَن يَسْبِقُونَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, that they will escape Us (yuʿjizūnā).

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَآءَ ٱللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ ٱللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is: whoever hopes to meet the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْناً﴾.
That is, what is good.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِن جَاهَدَاكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلاَ تُطِعْهُمَآ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: and if your parents strive against you, O man, to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يِقُولُ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is, when he was tormented, he feared the torment of people as he fears the torment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These were people who said "we believe", and when one of them was harmed he associated partners [with Allah].
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from ʿIkrima, who said: "There were people in Mecca who had borne witness that "there is no god but Allah". When the idolaters went out to Badr, they compelled them to go out with them, and some of them were killed. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning them: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَفَّاهُمُ المَلاَئِكَةُ ظَالِمي أَنْفُسِهِمْ قَالُوا فِيمَ كُنْتُمْ﴾ up to His saying ﴿فَأُوَلِئكَ عَسَى اللهُ أَنْ يَعْفُوَ عَنْهُمْ وكَانَ الله عَفُوَّاً غَفُورَاً﴾. The Muslims who were in Medina wrote it to the Muslims who were in Mecca. Then some Muslims went out of Mecca, the idolaters overtook them, and some of them succumbed to the trial; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning them: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يِقُولُ آمَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ فَإِذَآ أُوذِيَ فِي ٱللَّهِ جَعَلَ فِتْنَةَ ٱلنَّاسِ كَعَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ﴾."
Al-Shaʿbī said: Ten verses were revealed concerning them, from His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿الم. أحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوْا﴾. ʿIkrima said: The Muslims who were in Medina wrote them to the Muslims who were in Mecca. A man of Banū Ḍamra — who was ill — said: Take me out to relief (al-rawḥ). So they took him out, and he died; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed concerning him: ﴿وَمَنْ يَخْرُجْ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُهَاجِرَاً إلَى اللهِ وَرَسُوْلِهِ ثُمَّ يُدْرِكْهُ الْمَوْتُ فَقَدْ وقع أَجْرهُ عَلَى اللهِ﴾ to the end of the verse. And He revealed concerning the Muslims who had succumbed to the trial: ﴿ثم إنَّ ربَّكَ للَّذِينَ عملوا السُّوءَ بجهالةٍ ثم تابوا﴾ to the end of the verse.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ ٱتَّبِعُواْ سَبِيلَنَا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطَايَاكُمْ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: These are the leaders of the idolaters.
Mujāhid said: They are the idolaters of the people of Mecca; they said to those of them who believed: Neither we nor you will be resurrected, so follow us, and if there is any burden of sin upon you, it is upon us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is like your saying: "Put this on my neck if there is any sin in it", meaning: there is no sin in it.
Al-Farrāʾ said: It carries the sense of a conditional (mujāzāt), and he recited:
فقلْتُ ادْعِي وادْعُ فإنَّ أَنْدَى * لِصَوْتٍ أَنْ يُنَادَي دَاعِيانِ
(So I said: Call out, and let me call, for the farthest-carrying for a voice is that two callers cry out.)
He said: the meaning is "call, and let me call", that is: if you call, I will call.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا هُمْ بِحَامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾.
The meaning is: and they will not carry anything for them — that would lighten their load.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾.
Abū Umāma al-Bāhilī said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with many good deeds, and retribution will continue to be taken from him until his good deeds are exhausted [and then claims are made against him]. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, will say: Take retribution from My servant. The angels will say: He has no good deeds left. He will say: Take from the bad deeds of the wronged one and put them on him."
Abū Umāma said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿َوَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾:
He said: "Whoever calls to misguidance, its burden is written against him, along with the burden of whoever acts by it, without that diminishing anything from theirs."
Abū Jaʿfar said: The people of exegesis hold that the meaning of the verse is as Qatāda said; and similar to it is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾.
Anything abundant that encompasses everyone — rain, killing or death — is called ṭūfān.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾.
That is, and you carve.
The meaning on this view is: you only worship idols besides Allah, while you make them yourselves.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إفْكَاً﴾ means a lie.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [al-Sulamī] read ﴿وتَخَلَّقُوْنَ إفْكاً﴾, and the meaning is the same.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning is: nor whoever is in the heaven; and "مَنْ" is indefinite. Someone else recited:
فَمَنْ يَهْجُو رسُوْلَ اللهِ مِنكُمْ * وَيَمْدحُهُ ويَنْصُرهُ سَوَاءُ
(Is the one of you who lampoons the Messenger of Allah, and the one who praises and supports him, alike?)
[Translator's note: the verse is cited for the omission of a second «مَنْ» before ويمدحه.]
Someone other than Abū al-ʿAbbās said the meaning is: you cannot escape [Him] on earth, even if you were in the heaven; and people were addressed in terms of what they know.
This is more fitting, and Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ ٱقْتُلُوهُ أَوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأَنْجَاهُ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
The meaning is: so they burned him, and Allah saved him from the fire.
It is related that it burned nothing but his bonds.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَآمَنَ لَهُ لُوطٌ وَقَالَ إِنِّي مُهَاجِرٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّيۤ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Abraham emigrated, and he was the first to emigrate.
Qatāda said: He emigrated from Kūthā to Syria (al-Shām).

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Sufyān related from Ḥumayd ibn Qays, who said: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr told a man to ask ʿIkrima about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
ʿIkrima said: The followers of all the religions claim him and say: He is one of us. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: He has spoken truly.
Qatāda said: It is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾,
that is, well-being, righteous deeds and good praise; and that is because the people of every religion take him as their patron.
It has also been said: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾ means that most of the prophets are from his offspring.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلُوطاً إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
It is related that they were the first to mount men.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَئِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ ٱلرِّجَالَ وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
A question carrying the sense of rebuke and affirmation.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
It has been said: they used to intercept people on the roads for wickedness.
It has also been said: that is, you cut off the way of offspring.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: al-nādī is the assembly, and al-munkar (the abomination) is what they did with men.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-munkar in the language applies to obscene speech and to [obscene] action.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs ibn al-Aswad narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bakr narrated to us, saying: Ḥātim ibn Abī Ṣaghīra narrated to us, from Simāk, from Abū Ṣāliḥ — the freedman of Umm Hāniʾ daughter of Abū Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with her — that she asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She said: I said, O Messenger of Allah, what about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾: what was that abomination which they committed in their assembly? He said: They used to laugh at the passers-by and pelt them with pebbles.
Abū Jaʿfar said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, called this "an abomination" because people ought not to associate with one another in this way.
Usāma ibn Aḥmad narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, from Yazīd ibn Bukayr, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾: he said: They used to "yatafāʿalūna" in their gatherings, one of them doing it at another.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The shaykh said it with ḍād and ṭāʾ.
[Translator's note: the source writes the verb as the pattern word «يتفاعلون»; the remark that the shaykh pronounced it with ḍād and ṭāʾ indicates the actual word was «يتضارطون», i.e. they broke wind at one another.]

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطاً قَالُواْ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا﴾.
Abū Naṣr related from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Samura, who said: Abraham ﷺ said to the angels: If there are a hundred among them who hate this, will you destroy them?
They said: No.
He said: And if there are ninety among them? They said: No.
Until he reached twenty. ﴿قَالَ إِنَّ فِيهَا لُوطاً﴾, the angels, may Allah bless them, said: ﴿نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن فِيهَا﴾. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: And they numbered four hundred thousand.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطاً سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعاً﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, he thought ill of his people, and felt powerless on account of his guests.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is said ضِقْتُ به ذَرْعَاً, meaning "I could not bear it"; it is derived from al-dhirāʿ (the forearm), because strength lies in it.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَد تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ آيَةً بَيِّنَةً لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿آيَةً بَيِّنَةً﴾ means a lesson.
Qatāda said: It is the stones that were left remaining.
Someone else said: a people of this community will be stoned with them.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْباً﴾.
Qatāda said: Shuʿayb ﷺ was sent twice, to two nations: to the people of Madyan and to the Companions of the Thicket (al-Ayka).

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم مِّن مَّسَاكِنِهِمْ﴾.
That is, and We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd.
It has also been said: the implied wording (taqdīr) is: and remember ʿĀd and Thamūd.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, in error.
Qatāda said: that is, pleased with their error.
It has also been said: ﴿وَكَانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾ means they knew that they would be punished, and yet they did what they did.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمِنْهُم مَّن أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِباً﴾.
That is, ḥaṣab, which is stones; and they are the people of Lot.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلصَّيْحَةُ﴾: they are Thamūd and the people of Madyan.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ خَسَفْنَا بِهِ ٱلأَرْضَ﴾: Qārūn and his companions.
﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّنْ أَغْرَقْنَا﴾: the people of Noah, and Pharaoh and his companions.
Then He, Exalted is He, informed that He did not wrong them in that, saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَـٰكِن كَانُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتاً﴾.
Qatāda said: This is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck; that is, it is of no benefit because of its weakness, just as the spider's house neither benefits nor protects.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ ٱلْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿لَوْ﴾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying ﴿مَثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ﴾: if only they knew that their patrons avail them nothing, and that this is their likeness.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلاَةَ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلاَةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ﴾.
Yūnus related from al-Ḥasan, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever's prayer does not restrain him from indecency and abomination gains from it nothing but greater distance from Allah."
ʿAlī ibn Ṭalḥa related from Ibn Abī ʿAbbās, who said: In prayer there is a restraint and a deterrent from acts of disobedience.
[Translator's note: «ابن أبي عباس» is as written in the source; the usual chain is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from Ibn ʿAbbās.]
Abū Jaʿfar said: It has been said that the meaning of this is: as long as the servant is in prayer, he is not engaged in indecency or abomination.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ﴾.
Sufyān related from Ibn Masʿūd, and related from Salmān, and from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾: they said: Allah's remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him.
Ibn ʿAbbās added, after his words "of you": when you remember Him.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُجَادِلُوۤاْ أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَابِ إِلاَّ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنْهُمْ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid, who said: Whoever fights you and does not give you the jizya, fight him with the sword.
Maʿmar related from Qatāda, who said: It is abrogated; it was abrogated by ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِين حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾, and there is no disputation more severe than the sword.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Qatāda is closer to being correct, because the surah is Meccan, and fighting was only commanded after the Hijra, and the taking of the jizya was commanded a long time after that; and moreover He said ﴿وَهُمْ صَاغِرُونَ﴾.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾.
Sufyān related from Saʿd ibn Ibrāhīm, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Yasār, who said: "Some Jews used to sit with the Muslims and tell them things. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this, and he said to them: Neither believe them nor disbelieve them, ﴿وَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِٱلَّذِيۤ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse."

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُواْ مِن قَبْلِهِ مِن كِتَابٍ وَلاَ تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ﴾.
And such is his description, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِذاً لاَّرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: Quraysh.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ فِي صُدُورِ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْعِلْمَ﴾.
There are three views on its meaning:
a- Al-Ḥasan said: Rather, the Qurʾan is clear signs in the breasts of the believers.
b- Qatāda said: Rather, the Prophet ﷺ is a clear sign; thus Qatāda read: "فِي صُدُوْرِ الَّذِينَ أُوْتُوا العِلْمَ، من أهل الكتاب" (in the breasts of those given knowledge, of the People of the Book).
c- Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: The description of the Prophet ﷺ was that he would not write with his right hand nor recite a book, and that is a clear sign.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār from Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿda, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ was brought a shoulder-blade with writing on it, and he said: It is enough folly — or misguidance — for a people that they turn away from their prophet to a prophet other than him, or to a book other than their book." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (the verse).

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَٱعْبُدُونِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: When you are commanded to commit acts of disobedience, flee.
ʿAṭāʾ said: When you see acts of disobedience, flee.
Mujāhid said: Emigrate and keep away from the idols.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The two views come back to one thing: Mujāhid's view is that they were commanded to emigrate and to shun the idol-worshippers. And the scholars said: likewise, when one is unable to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, he should leave, and his ruling is the ruling of those.
It has also been said: that is, the land of Paradise is vast, so worship Me so that I may give it to you.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ غُرَفَاً﴾.
That is, We will surely lodge them.
And the meaning of ﴿لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم﴾ is: We will surely give them dwellings in which they abide; it is said ثَوَى when one resides.
[Translator's note: ﴿لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم﴾ is a variant reading of ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾; the source does not name its readers here.]

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ لاَّ تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: Birds and beasts do not carry their provision.
Al-Ḥumaydī related from Sufyān: ﴿لاَّ تَحْمِلُ﴾ means it does not store away. He said: Nothing stores up except man, the ant and the mouse.
Abū Jaʿfar said: ﴿دَآبَّةٍ﴾ applies to every living creature, rational and non-rational, except that its meaning here is restricted: that is, how many a helpless creature there is that Allah provides for, as well as you.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: There is no death in it.
Qatāda said: al-ḥayawān is life.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ḥayawān, ḥayāh and ḥiyy, as [the poet] said:
* "وقد تَرَى إذِ الحَيَاةُ حِيُّ" *
(and you used to see, when life was alive…)
[Translator's note: the source has «قتال أبو جعفر», evidently a slip for «قال أبو جعفر».]

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ دَعَوُاْ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is, when hardship befalls them, they call on Allah alone and abandon what they worship besides Him.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْبَرِّ إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
That is, they call upon others along with Him.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ آتَيْنَاهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ يَعلَمُونَ﴾.
﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُواْ﴾ is by way of threat, with kasra on the lām.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَاهَدُواْ فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا﴾.
That is, We will surely increase them in guidance.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed us that He will help them, saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمَعَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) is for interrogation. (أن) is a particle of the maṣdar (verbal noun) and of the accusative. The (الواو) in (يتركوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتركوا ... ) is in the position of the accusative, standing in the place of the two objects of حسب.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقولوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive, through an omitted lām, attached to (يتركوا) «[Note: or in the position of the genitive through an omitted bāʾ, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the deputy agent, i.e. "holding fast to their saying: We believe".]» . (الواو) is circumstantial. (لا) is negative, and the (الواو) in (يفتنون) is the deputy agent.
The clause «حسب الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «يتركوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يقولوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «آمنّا ... » is in the position of the accusative, being the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «هم لا يفتنون.» is in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يفتنون ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(3) (الواو) is a conjunction. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (قد) is a particle of affirmation. (من قبلهم) is attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative. (الفاء) is a conjunction, and likewise (الواو); (اللام) is the lām of the oath for an implied oath, in both places. (يعلمنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative. (الذين) is a relative noun, direct object, in the position of the accusative.
The clause «فتنّا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the opening clause.
The clause «يعلمنّ (the first) » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first implied oath clause.
The clause «يعلمنّ ... (the second) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the first clause يعلمنّ «[Note: or it is the response to the implied oath, and the oath clause is conjoined to the first oath clause.]» .

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of address): in the words of Allah the Exalted فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ.
The shift to the majestic name is to instil awe, to build reverence, and to repeat the response, for added emphasis and affirmation; that is: "By Allah, His knowledge will indeed attach to the trial, an attachment in the present, by which those who were truthful in the faith they displayed are distinguished, and those who are liars in it, persisting in the lie; and their recompense of reward and punishment follows upon it."
Expression by the verbal form and the nominal form: in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكاذِبِينَ» there is a contrast between the verbal form, «صدقوا», and the nominal form in His words «الكاذبين». The point of this contrast is that the active participle indicates that the verbal noun is established in the agent and firmly rooted in him, whereas the past verb does not indicate that. For at the time the verse was revealed it was a report about a people who were close to the time of their entry into Islam, and about a people persisting in disbelief; so for the former He expressed it with the verb, and for the latter with the form that indicates permanence.

* Benefits:
- Verbs of the heart.
Verbs of the heart are divided into three kinds:
a- Those that do not govern an object by themselves, and must have a preposition through which they govern, e.g. فكر في الأمر ("he reflected on the matter").
b- Those that govern one object, directly, e.g. عرف الحق ("he knew the truth") and فهم المسألة ("he understood the question").
c- Those that govern two objects directly, whose origin is a mubtadaʾ and khabar. Zufar ibn al-Ḥārith al-Kilābī says:
وكنا حسبنا كل بيضاء شحمة ... عشية لاقينا جذام وحميرا
(We had reckoned every white thing to be fat, on the evening we met Judhām and Ḥimyar.)
That is, he used to think them brave men, but they turned out to be otherwise.
And finally, we hope the meaning of the verse has become clear, namely: Do those who were quick to utter the testimony of faith consider it easy and exalt themselves over others by it, [thinking] that they will be left without being tested? Rather, Allah will try them with various kinds of trials and tribulations. For faith is not words repeated on the tongues without being supported by deeds and mingled with minds and hearts.

safi-cedvel:5-7.t:
* I'rab:
(كان) is a defective past verb, in the position of the jussive, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اللام) is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (آت) is the khabar of inna, nominative, its sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ. (الواو) is resumptive. (العليم) is a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «من كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان يرجو ... » is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّ أجل الله ... » has no grammatical position; it gives the reason for the implied apodosis, i.e.: "let him prepare for it, because the term of Allah is coming".
The clause «هو السميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(6) (الواو) is a conjunction. (من جاهد) is like من كان. (الفاء) is the connective of the apodosis. (إنّما) is a restrictive particle (kāffa) and what it restricts (makfūfa). (لنفسه) is attached to (يجاهد). (اللام) is the shifted lām, for emphasis. (عن العالمين) is attached to غنيّ.
The clause «من جاهد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من كان.
The clause «جاهد» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «إنّما يجاهد ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis, accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله لغنيّ ... » has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
(7) (الواو) is a conjunction in the three places. (اللام) is the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (نكفّرنّ) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative, and the agent is "we", for glorification. (عنهم) is attached to (نكفّرنّ). (لنجزينّهم) is like (لنكفرنّ). (الذي) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «الذين آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من جاهد.
