Clause: «انصرني ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لمّا) an adverb with the sense of "when", containing the sense of a condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis قالوا (بالبشرى) attached to a ḥāl of the agent of جاءت or of its object (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb (inna), and its ism is (القرية) a badal for هذه - or an ʿaṭf bayān -.
Clause: «جاءت رسلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «إنّا مهلكو ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّ أهلها كانوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.
Clause: «كانوا ظالمين» is in the position of a nominative, the predicate of إنّ.

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(فيها) attached to the predicate of إنّ (بمن) attached to أعلم (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (ننجّينّه) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (أهله) conjoined to the pronoun object (in ننجّينّه), accusative (إلّا) a particle of exception (امرأته) accusative as the excepted (من الغابرين) attached to the predicate of كانت.
Clause: «قال ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «إنّ فيها لوطا ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
Clause: «نحن أعلم ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «ننجّينّه ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ... and the clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is a resumption within the scope of the quoted speech.
Clause: «كانت من الغابرين ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Rhetoric:
The art of allusion (fann al-ishāra): in the saying of the Exalted إِنَّ فِيها لُوطاً.
The aim is not to inform them that he is in it, but rather it is a dispute about his case: for when they justified the destruction of its people by their wrongdoing, he objected to them that in it was one who was free of wrongdoing. By the dispute he intended to show compassion for them, and what is due from a believer, grieving for his brother, bestirring himself to support and protect him, and fearing that harm touch him or injury reach him. This is among the eloquent and subtle allusions.

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (عادا) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being (أهلكنا), and the agent of (تبيّن) is a latent pronoun referring to the destruction understood from the context of the verse (لكم) attached to (تبيّن), (من مساكنهم) attached to (تبيّن), (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl - or resumptive (لهم) attached to (زيّن), (الفاء) a conjunction (عن السبيل) attached to (ضدّهم), (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl.
Clause: « (أهلكنا) ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «تبيّن ... (إهلاكهم)» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical «[Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.]».
Clause: «زيّن لهم الشيطان ...» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, with (قد) implied «[Note: or has no grammatical position, being resumptive.]».
Clause: «صدّهم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause زيّن لهم الشيطان.
Clause: «كانوا مستبصرين» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.

* Morphology:
(مستبصرين), plural of مستبصر, an active participle from the sextriliteral (sudāsī) استبصر; its wazn is مستفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:39-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction in all three places (قارون) conjoined to (عادا) «[Note: in the preceding verse (38).]», (الواو) resumptive (لقد جاءهم موسى) like لقد تركنا «[Note: in verse (35) of this sūra.]», (بالبيّنات) attached to a ḥāl of موسى (الفاء) a conjunction (في الأرض) attached to (استكبروا) (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation.
Clause: «جاءهم موسى ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath ...
The clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «استكبروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the oath.
Clause: «ما كانوا سابقين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the oath.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive (كلّا) a fronted direct object, accusative (بذنبه) attached to (أخذنا), and the bāʾ expresses cause (الفاء) a conjunction of consequence (tafrīʿ) (منهم) attached to a fronted predicate of the delayed subject (من أرسلنا) «[Note: it may be an adjective of an omitted subject, its implied form being "some of them", in which case the predicate is the relative.]», (عليه) attached to (أرسلنا), and the following similar clauses are parsed likewise (به) attached to (خسفنا), (الواو) a conjunction (ما) a negation (اللام) the lām of denial (juḥūd) or disavowal (يظلمهم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām (الواو) a conjunction (أنفسهم) a fronted direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يظلمهم ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted predicate of كان.
Clause: «أخذنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
Clause: «منهم من أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من أخذته ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «أخذته الصيحة ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من خسفنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «خسفنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative (من).
Clause: «منهم من أغرقنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من أرسلنا.
Clause: «أغرقنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the fourth relative (من).
Clause: «ما كان الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
Clause: «يظلمهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
Clause: «كانوا ... يظلمون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ما كان الله ليظلمهم.
Clause: «يظلمون» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كانوا.

* Benefits:
- كلا is a fronted direct object of the verb «أخذنا ...»; we have already spoken of كل and بعض earlier.
- وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ: this lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), whose definition is that it is preceded by a negated كون, and it has already been discussed.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لمّا ... لوطا) like لمّا ...
إبراهيم «[Note: in verse (31) of this sūra.]», (أن) redundant, and the deputy agent of the verb (سيء) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), that is Lot «[Note: it is permissible that the pronoun refer to the maṣdar of the verb, with the sense "distress came to him".]», (بهم) attached to (سيء), and the bāʾ expresses cause (بهم) the second, attached to (ضاق) (ذرعا) a specification (tamyīz), accusative, transformed from an agent, that is: "his capacity was constrained by them" (الواو) a conjunction in all three places (لا) a prohibitive that jusses, in both places (إنّا منجّوك) like إنّا مهلكو ..., (أهلك) a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "we will save" «[Note: this is according to the opinion of Sībawayh; al-Akhfash permits the conjoining of the noun to the position of the kāf in (منّجوك), because its position is genitive and accusative.]», (إلّا ... الغابرين) like إلّا امرأته كانت من الغابرين «[Note: in verse (32) of this sūra.]».
Clause: «جاءت رسلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «سيء بهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
Clause: «ضاق بهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيء بهم.
Clause: «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيء بهم.
Clause: «لا تخف ...» is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «لا تحزن ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the quoted speech.
Clause: «إنّا منجّوك ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification.
Clause: «كانت من الغابرين» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
(34) (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its ism (على أهل) attached to (منزلون), (جزاء) a direct object of the active participle منزلون (من السماء) attached to an adjective of (رجزا), (ما) a maṣdar particle ...
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the active participle منزلون, and the bāʾ expresses cause.
Clause: «إنّا منزلون ...» has no grammatical position; it is a justification of the saving.
Clause: «كانوا يفسقون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).
Clause: «يفسقون» is in the position of an accusative, the predicate of كانوا.
(35) (الواو) a conjunction (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (منها) attached to (تركنا), (لقوم) attached to بيّنة «[Note: it may be attached to (تركنا), or to آية.]».
Clause: «تركنا» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the implied oath.
Clause: «يعقلون» is in the position of a genitive, an adjective of قوم.

* Morphology:
(سيء): apparently the alif was changed to yāʾ for conformity with the passive form; its origin was ساء. But the change occurred on the wāw; its imperfect is يسوء, so the origin of the word in the passive was سوئ with ḍamma on the sīn and kasra on the wāw; then the wāw was made sākin because of the heaviness of the kasra and the kasra was moved to the sīn; then the wāw was changed to yāʾ because what precedes it is kasra, and it became سيء. This is the way of the hollow verb whose middle letter is wāw.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction - or resumptive - (إلى مدين) attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We sent" (شعيبا) an ʿaṭf bayān - or a badal - accusative (الفاء) a conjunction (قوم) a vocative, a muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on what precedes the yāʾ, omitted for lightness ... and the (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction in both places (لا) a prohibitive that jusses (في الأرض) attached to the verb تعثوا (مفسدين) a confirmatory ḥāl, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
Clause: « (أرسلنا) ... شعيبا» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the implied oath «[Note: in the preceding verse (35), or it is resumptive.]».
Clause: «قال» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أرسلنا.
The clause of the vocative and its response is in the position of an accusative, being the quoted speech.
Clause: «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
Clause: «ارجوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
Clause: «لا تعثوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
(37) (الفاء) a conjunction in all three places (في دارهم) attached to (جاثمين), the predicate of أصبحوا.
Clause: «كذّبوه ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause قال.
Clause: «أخذتهم الرجفة ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوه.
Clause: «أصبحوا ... جاثمين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أخذتهم الرجفة.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {أَن يتركوا}: it fills the place of the two objects of حَسِب according to the majority, and the place of one of them according to al-Akhfash.
His saying: «أنْ يقولوا»: there are several views in it. The first: that it is a badal (substitute) from «أَنْ يُتْرَكوا», an interpreted maṣdar substituted from its like. The second: that it is by dropping the preposition (bi-isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), which is the bāʾ or the lām, i.e. "for saying" or "because they say". Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "If the bāʾ is assumed, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial)." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning with the bāʾ and the lām differs: with the bāʾ it is as you say 'I left Zayd in his state', and with the lām it means 'for the sake of', i.e. did they think that their faith is a cause for being left?" End quote. This is an explanation of meaning; had he explained the i'rab he would have said: "Is their thinking [themselves] left because of their uttering faith?"
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: where is the speech that indicates the content required by the thinking (ḥusbān)? I say: it is in His saying {أَن يتركوا أَن يقولوا: آمَنَّا، وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ}. That is because its implied form is: 'Did they think their being left unafflicted [was] because of their saying "We believe"?' So the leaving is the first of the two objects of «حَسِب», and 'because of their saying "We believe"' is the khabar (predicate). As for 'unafflicted', it is the complement of the leaving, because it is of the leaving that means rendering (taṣyīr), as in his saying:
3633 - فَتَرَكْتُه جَزَرَ السِّباعِ يَنُشْنَه ... . . . . . . . . . .
(So I left him as slaughter-meat for the beasts of prey, which tear at him…)
Do you not see that, before bringing in the thinking, you can say: 'their being left unafflicted is because of their saying "We believe"', on the [assumption] of 'occurring' and 'settled' before the lām? If you say: «أَنْ يَقُولوا» is the cause of their being left unafflicted, so how can it validly occur as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ? I say: as you say 'his going out is for fear of evil' and 'his beating is for discipline', whereas discipline and fear in your saying 'I went out for fear of evil' and 'I beat him for discipline' were two causes. And you also say: 'I thought his going out was for fear of evil' and 'I supposed his beating was for discipline', making them two objects just as you made them a mubtadaʾ and khabar." [Translator's note: the verse number 3633 here repeats the number already given above (in the entry on al-Qaṣaṣ 68); kept as written.]
The Shaykh said after all this: "It is speech in which there is confusion. He first mentioned that its implied 'unafflicted' is a complement, meaning that it is a ḥāl, because he cast that from His saying {وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ}, which is a circumstantial clause; then he mentioned that «يُتْركوا» here is of the leaving which is rendering. That is not sound, because the second object of «صيَّر» cannot properly be «لقولِهم», since the implied form would become: 'that they be rendered because of their saying, while they are not afflicted', and this is speech that is not sound. As for the verse he exemplified it with, «جَزَرَ السِّباع» may validly be the second object of تَرَكَ in the sense of صَيَّر, unlike what he assumed in the verse. As for his assuming 'their being left unafflicted is because of their saying [We believe]', on the assumption of 'occurring' and 'settled' before the lām, it is not sound if 'their being left' means 'their being rendered' and 'unafflicted' is a ḥāl, since no mubtadaʾ and khabar can be formed from 'their being left' in the sense of 'their being rendered' and 'their saying', because 'their being left' in the sense of 'their being rendered' needs a second object, since 'unafflicted' for him is a ḥāl, not a second object.
As for his saying 'If you say: «أَنْ يقولوا» …' to the end, it needs extra understanding: his saying that «أَنْ يقولوا» is the cause of their being left is not so, because had it been a cause of it, it would have been attached to it as it is attached to the verb; rather it is a cause of the omitted khabar, which is 'settled' or 'being', and the khabar is other than the mubtadaʾ. Had «لقولِهم» been a cause of the leaving, it would have been part of it and would have needed a khabar. As for his saying 'as you say: his going out is for fear of evil', «لمخافة» is not a cause of the going out but of the omitted khabar, which is 'settled' or 'being'." End quote.
I say: the answer to all that the Shaykh has mentioned is that al-Zamakhsharī only looked to the side of meaning, and his words are sound on that basis. As for his saying "it is not a cause of the going out" and the like, he means in wording; as for meaning, it is certainly a cause of it. And were it not for fear of departing from the purpose… [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off here in the source; translated as written.]

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الله الذين صَدَقُواْ}: the generality read it with fatḥa on the yāʾ, the imperfect of «عَلِم» which is transitive to one object — so they said. There is a difficulty in it that has been raised more than once: when it is transitive to one object it means عَرَفَ ("to come to know"), and this meaning may not be attributed to the Creator, the Exalted, because it requires prior ignorance, and because it relates only to the essence, not to the states in which it is.
ʿAlī and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the imperfect of أَعْلَم. It may be from عَلِم meaning عَرَفَ; when the hamza of transfer was brought, it gave it another object, which was omitted. Then this object may be the first, i.e. "Allah will surely make known to people the truthful, and make known to them the liars", i.e. by a renown by which these are distinguished from those; or it may be the second, i.e. "He will surely make known to these their stations, and to those their stations in the Hereafter". It may also be from العلامة, which is the mark (sīmiyāʾ), in which case it is transitive only to one object, i.e. "We will surely make for them a mark by which they are known". Al-Zuhrī read the first like the well-known reading and the second like the irregular one.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {أم حَسِبَ}: this «أم» is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), and so it is estimated as بل plus the hamza according to the majority; the digression (iḍrāb) is a transition, not a cancellation. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«أم» is the counterpart of the alif in His saying «أَحَسِبَ», as though He, Mighty and Majestic, made both parties acknowledge: He made the believers acknowledge [their thinking that they] will not be tried, and the disbelievers that they will outstrip Allah's punishment." The Shaykh said: "It is not a counterpart, since had it been so it would be conjunctive (muttaṣila), and it cannot be conjunctive for the lack of two conditions. The first: what follows it is not a single word or what is equivalent to one. The second: there is nothing here that is answered by one of two or more things."
Al-Zamakhsharī permitted this «حَسِبَ» to be transitive to two objects, making «أنَّ» and what falls within its scope fill their place, as in His saying {أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُواْ الجنة} [al-Baqara: 214]; or to be transitive to one, on the view that it contains the meaning of «قَدَّر» ("to reckon"). However, implication (taḍmīn) is not regular.
His saying: {سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ}: «ساء» may mean بِئْس, and then «ما» is either a relative meaning الذي, with «يَحْكمون» its ṣila (relative clause), and it is the fāʿil (agent) of «ساء», the one specified for blame being omitted, i.e. "their judgement". Or «ما» may be a tamyīz (specification), «يَحْكُمون» its adjective, and the agent a latent pronoun explained by «ما», the one specified also omitted. Or «ما» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival), which is the view of Ibn Kaysān; on this the tamyīz is omitted and the interpreted maṣdar is the one specified for blame, i.e. "evil as a judgement is their judgement". The ruling on «ما» when joined to «بِئْسَ» has preceded fully in al-Baqara. «ساء» may also mean قَبُح ("is ugly"), in which case «ما» may be maṣdariyya, or mean الذي, or be an indefinite qualified noun. «يَحْكمون» was used rather than "they judged" either to point out that this is their habit, or because it stands in place of the past for the sake of the verse-ending.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {مَن كَانَ}: it may be conditional or relative, the fāʾ [then being] because of its resemblance to the conditional. The apparent view is that this is not the apodosis, because Allah's term is coming inevitably without being restricted by a condition; rather the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "let him do righteous work and associate no one in the worship of his Lord", as He has stated explicitly.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being the omitted oath clause and its answer, i.e. "By Allah, We will surely expiate". It may be accusative by an implied verb by way of occupation (ishtighāl), i.e. "We will surely free those who believe from their misdeeds".
His saying: {أَحْسَنَ الذي كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}: it has been said: with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "the reward of the best". What is meant by «أَحْسَن» here is mere description. It has been said: so that it does not follow that their reward for the good is passed over in silence. This is nothing, because it is a fortiori: if He rewards them for the best, He rewards them for what is below it; so it is of pointing to the lower through the higher. His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the accusative by way of ishtighāl are both possible in it.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {حُسْناً}: there are several views in it. The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a good enjoining" — either by way of hyperbole, being made goodness itself, or with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessing goodness". The second: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "There is figurative usage in that; the original is: 'We enjoined on man goodness in his conduct with his parents'. Similar to this is the poet's saying:
3634 - عَجِبْتُ مِنْ دَهْماءَ إذ تَشْكُوْنا ... ومِنْ أبي دَهْماءَ إذ يُوصِيْنا
خيراً بنا كأنَّنا جافُونا ...
(I marvelled at Dahmāʾ when she complained of us, and at Dahmāʾ's father when he enjoined good to us concerning her, as though we had been harsh to her.)
and like it the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
3635 - وَصَّيْتُ مِنْ بَرَّةَ قلباً حُرَّاً ... بالكَلْبِ خيراً والحَماةِ شَرَّاً
(I enjoined upon a noble heart from Barra good towards the dog and evil towards the mother-in-law.)
On this the original is: 'We enjoined him with goodness in the matter of his parents'; then the parents were put in the genitive with the bāʾ, and «حُسْناً» became accusative; likewise the two verses. The bāʾ in the verse and the two verses in this case is locative." [Translator's note: the source numbers these verses «363 - 4-» and «363 - 5-», i.e. 3634 and 3635.]
The third: that «بوالديه» is the second object, and «حُسْناً» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "he does good, a doing of good", so it is an emphatic maṣdar. So it has been said; and there is room for consideration in it, because the governor of an emphatic [maṣdar] is not omitted. The fourth: that it is a direct object by implication (taḍmīn), i.e. "We obliged him [to] goodness". The fifth: that it is by dropping the preposition, i.e. "with goodness"; the author of al-Taḥrīr expressed that as "cutting off" (qaṭʿ). The sixth: that some of the Kufans estimated it as "We enjoined on man that he do good to his parents"; in this there is omission of «أنْ» and its ṣila with retention of what it governs, which is not permissible according to the Basrans. The seventh: that the implied form is "We enjoined on him giving his parents goodness"; in this there is omission of the maṣdar with retention of what it governs, which is not permissible. The eighth: that it is accusative in the same way as «زيداً» in your saying to someone you see preparing to strike: «زيداً», i.e. "strike Zayd!"; the implied form here is "show them goodness" or "do goodness to them". Al-Zamakhsharī said these two.
ʿĪsā and al-Jaḥdarī read «حَسَناً» with two fatḥas; they are two dialectal forms, like البُخْل and البَخَل. That has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {لَيَقُولُنَّ}: the generality read it with ḍamma on the lām, attributing the verb to a plural pronoun, construing according to the meaning of «مَنْ» after it was construed according to its wording. Abū Muʿādh the grammarian reported that it was read «لَيَقُولَنَّ» with fatḥa, likewise continuing in regard to its wording. The reading of the generality is better because of His saying «إنَّا كُنَّا».

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَلْنَحْمِلْ}: an imperative with the meaning of a statement. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read it with kasra on the lām of the imperative, which is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This was the saying of the chieftains of Quraysh; they used to say to those of them who believed: 'Neither we nor you will be resurrected; and if perhaps that should be (fa-in ʿasā kāna dhālika), then we will bear [your sins].'" The Shaykh said: "It is a non-Arab construction, in respect of introducing the conditional particle onto «عسى», which is inflexible (jāmida), using it without a noun or a predicate, and making كان follow it."
The generality read «خطاياكُمْ» as a broken plural. Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind [read] «مِنْ خَطِيْئاتهم» as a sound plural; from him also «خَطيئتِهم» in the singular, meaning the genus — this resembles the two readings of {وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خطيائته} [al-Baqara: 81] and «خطيئاته». From him also «خَطَئِهم»; it has been said: with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and kasra on the yāʾ, meaning with kasra on the hamza that is close to yāʾ, because of its being lightened "between-between" (bayna bayna).
And «مِنْ شيء» is the object of «حامِلين», and «مِنْ خطاياهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; since it precedes it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ}: accusative as an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi). {إِلاَّ خَمْسِينَ عَاماً} is accusative as an exception. There is disagreement over the occurrence of exception from number nouns, and those who forbid it have an answer regarding this verse. A fine subtle point has been observed here: He varied between the tamyīz (specification) of the two numbers, saying in the first «سَنَة» and in the second «عاماً», so that the wording would not be heavy. Then He assigned the word «عام» to the fifty, to indicate that Allah's Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, once relieved of them, remained in a good time; the Arabs express fertility by العام and drought by السَّنَة.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاهَآ}, i.e. the punishment, or the flood, or the like.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ}: the generality read it in the accusative, conjoined to «نوحاً», or by an implied "remember", or conjoined to the hāʾ of «أَنْجَيْناه». Al-Nakhaʿī, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Ḥanīfa [read] «وإبراهيمُ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being implied, i.e. "and among the messengers is Abraham".
His saying: «إذ قالَ» is a badal (substitute) from «إبراهيمَ», a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl).

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {وَتَخْلُقُونَ}: the generality [read it] with fatḥa on the tāʾ, sukūn on the khāʾ and sukūn on the lām [Translator's note: as written in the source; in the common reading the lām carries a ḍamma], the imperfect of خَلَقَ, with «إفكاً» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the fāʾ, i.e. "and you fabricate lies" or "you carve idols". ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Sulamī and Qatāda [read it] with fatḥa on the khāʾ and on the lām, doubled; it is the imperfect of «تَخَلَّقَ», the original being تَتَخَلَّقُوْن with two tāʾs, one of which was deleted, as in تَنزَّلُ and the like. It is also narrated from Zayd ibn ʿAlī «تُخَلِّقُوْن», with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled lām, the imperfect of the doubled خَلَّق.
Ibn al-Zubayr and Fuḍayl ibn Zurqān read «أَفِكاً», with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on the fāʾ; it is a maṣdar like الكَذِب in meaning and pattern. Al-Zamakhsharī permitted two views for الإِفْك with kasra and sukūn. The first: that it is lightened from الأَفِك with fatḥa and kasra, like الكِذْب and اللِّعْب, whose originals are الكَذِب and اللَّعِب. [The second:] that it is an adjective of the pattern فِعْل, i.e. "a false creation", i.e. "possessing falsehood". I say: his assuming a muḍāf before إفك while making it an adjective is unnecessary; it would only be needed if he made it a maṣdar.
His saying: «رِزْقاً»: it may be accusative as a maṣdar, its governor being «لا يَمْلِكون», because it is in its sense. On the principles of the Kufans, the original may be "they are not able to provide you a provision", so «أَنْ يَرْزُقوكم» is the object of «يَمْلكون». It may also mean "what is provided", so it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {يَرَوْاْ كَيْفَ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Abū Bakr read it in the second person, as Abraham's addressing his people with that; the rest in the third person, referring back to the denying nations.
His saying: «كيف يُبْدِئُ»: the generality read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from أَبْدَأَ. Al-Zubayrī, ʿĪsā and Abū ʿAmr — with a disagreement [in transmission] from him — [read] «يَبْدَأُ», the imperfect of بدأ; its past has been stated explicitly here where He said {كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الخلق} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 20]. Al-Zuhrī read «كيف بَدا» with a plain alif; it is an irregular lightening, its regular form being "between-between" (bayna bayna). In irregularity it is like his saying:
3636 - . . . . . . . . . . ... فَارْعَيْ فَزارةُ لا هَناكِ المَرْتَعُ
(…so graze, Fazāra — may the pasture not be wholesome for you!)

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {النشأة}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «النَّشاءةَ» with lengthening here, in al-Najm and in al-Wāqiʿa; the rest with the short form and sukūn on the shīn. They are two dialectal forms, like الرَّأْفة and الرَّآفة. Their being accusative is as a maṣdar with its additional letters dropped, the original being الإِنشاءة; or by omission of the governor, i.e. "He originates, so they originate an origination". It is written with an alif, and that strengthens the reading with lengthening.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ فِي السمآء}: on the supposition that they were in it, as in His saying {إِنِ استطعتم أَن تَنفُذُواْ مِنْ أَقْطَارِ السماوات} [al-Raḥmān: 33], i.e. on the supposition that they were in it. Ibn Zayd and al-Farrāʾ said: "Its meaning is: nor whoever is in the heaven, i.e. can escape [Him] if he disobeys" — meaning that "whoever is in the heavens" is conjoined to «أنتم», with the implied "if he disobeys". Al-Farrāʾ said: "This is one of the obscure points of Arabic." I say: this is according to his principle, since he permits the omission of the nominal relative while its ṣila remains. He recited:
3637 - أمَن يهْجُو رسولَ الله منكُمْ ... ويَنْصُرُه ويَمْدَحُه سَواءُ
(Is the one of you who satirizes the Messenger of Allah, and [the one who] supports him and praises him, equal?)
More remote than that is whoever assumed two omitted relatives, i.e. "You cannot escape [from] whoever is on the earth of humans and jinn, nor whoever is in the heaven of the angels; so how could you escape their Creator?" On the view of the majority, the object is omitted, i.e. "you are not able to escape", i.e. to evade what Allah wills for you.
His saying: «ثم يُعيدُه» and {ثُمَّ الله يُنشِىءُ} are both resumptive, of Allah the Exalted's informing; so the first is not included within the scope of the seeing, nor the second within the scope of the looking.
[Translator's note: the final paragraph, on «ثم يعيده» and «ثم الله ينشئ», pertains to verses 19–20, though it appears under this entry in the source.]

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {فَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ قَوْمِهِ}: the generality read it in the accusative; al-Ḥasan and Sālim al-Afṭas in the nominative. The verification of this has preceded.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {إِنَّمَا اتخذتم}: in this «ما» there are three views. The first: that it is a relative meaning الذي, the referent pronoun being omitted — it is the first object — and «أَوْثاناً» the second object. The khabar (predicate) is «مَوَدَّةُ» in the reading of those who put it in the nominative, as will come; the implied form is: "that which you have taken as idols is affection", i.e. "a matter of affection", or it was made affection itself. And it is omitted in the reading of those who put «مَوَدَّةَ» in the accusative, i.e. "that which you have taken as idols for the sake of affection will not benefit you" or "will be against you", indicated by His saying {ثُمَّ يَوْمَ القيامة يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ}.
The second: that «ما» is made restrictive-cancelling (kāffa) and «أوثاناً» a direct object. The taking here is transitive to one object, or to two, the second being {مِّن دُونِ الله}. Whoever puts «مودةُ» in the nominative makes it the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is affection", i.e. "possessing affection", or it was made affection itself by way of hyperbole; the clause is then an adjective of «أَوْثاناً» or resumptive. Whoever puts it in the accusative makes it a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or [accusative] by an implied "I mean".
The third: that «ما» is made maṣdariyya (infinitival). In that case a muḍāf may be assumed in the first part, i.e. "the cause of your taking idols is affection", for those who read «مودةُ» in the nominative; or it may not be assumed, the taking itself being made the affection by way of hyperbole. In the reading of those who put it in the accusative, the khabar is omitted, as passed in the first view.
Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «مودةُ» in the nominative without tanwīn and «بَيْنِكم» in the genitive. Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr [read] «مودةً» in the accusative with tanwīn and «بينَكم» in the accusative. Ḥamza and Ḥafṣ [read] «مودةَ» in the accusative without tanwīn and «بَيْنِكم» in the genitive. The nominative has been dealt with. The accusative too has been dealt with, with two views; a third view is possible, which is that it be made a second object by way of hyperbole, the annexation being by latitude with the adverbial, as in their saying:
3638 - يا سارِقَ الليلةِ أهلَ الدارِ ...
(O you who rob the people of the house on this night [lit. "O robber of the night, the people of the house"].)
Whoever put it in the accusative did so according to its original [status]. It is transmitted from ʿĀṣim that he read «مودةُ» in the nominative without tanwīn and «بينَكم» in the accusative; it has been explained on the basis of annexing «مودةُ» to the adverbial, which was only made indeclinable because it is annexed to something non-declinable, like the reading {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] with fatḥa if we make «بينَكم» the agent.
As for «في الحياة», there are [several views] in it. The first: that it and «بينَكم» are both attached to «مودَّة» when it has tanwīn; it is permissible for both to be attached to one governor because they differ. The second: that they are both attached to something omitted, as two adjectives of «مودَّة». The third: that «بَيْنَكم» is attached to «مودَّة» and «في الحياة» is an adjective of «مودة»; the reverse is not permissible, lest it entail the governance of a maṣdar that has been qualified. The difference between it and the first is that in the first the maṣdar governed it before being qualified, while here it governed it after being qualified.
However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others permitted that, as though they allowed latitude with the adverbial; so this is a fourth view.
The fifth: that «في الحياة» is attached to «بينَكم» itself, because it has the sense of the verb, since the implied form is "your coming together and your union". The sixth: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بينَكم» itself. The seventh: that «بينَكم» is an adjective of «مودة» and «في الحياة» a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in it. The eighth: that «في الحياة» is attached to «اتَّخذتُمْ», on the view that «ما» is kāffa and «مودة» accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lest it lead to separation between the relative and what is in the ṣila by the khabar."

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {وَلُوطاً}: like His saying {وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 16].
His saying: «ما سَبَقكم»: it may be resumptive, as an answer to someone who asked about that, or circumstantial, i.e. "originating it".

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَلَمَّآ أَن جَآءَتْ}: its parallel has preceded, except that here «أَنْ» has been added, which is regular, for emphasis.
His saying: «إنَّا مُنَجُّوك»: regarding the kāf and the like there are two doctrines. The doctrine of Sībawayh: that it is in the position of a genitive; on this there are two views on the accusative of «وأهلَكَ»: an implied verb, or conjunction to the position. The doctrine of al-Akhfash and Hishām: that it is in the position of an accusative, and the tanwīn and the nūn were dropped because of the strong attachment of the pronoun.
The two readings with the light and doubled [jīm] in «لنُنَجِّيَنَّه» and «مُنَجُّوك» have preceded in al-Ḥijr.

semin-durr:34-34.t: «مُنْزِلون» was read both light and doubled. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «رُجْزاً» with ḍamma on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿmash and Abū Ḥaywa [read] «يَفْسِقون» with kasra.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {تَّرَكْنَا مِنْهَآ آيَةً}: there are two views in it. The first: that part of it remains, and it is a sign that remains to this day. The second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida); al-Farrāʾ inclined to this, i.e. "We left it as a sign", as in his saying:
3639 - أمْهَرْت مِنْها جُبَّة وتَيْسا ...
(I gave her as dowry a cloak and a he-goat.)
i.e. "I gave her as dowry". This comes on the view of al-Akhfash. [Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as «363 - 9-», i.e. 3639.]

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وإلى مَدْيَنَ}, i.e. "and We sent", or "We dispatched", to Madyan their brother. And «شُعَيباً» is a badal (substitute), or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or [accusative] by an implied "I mean".

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {وَعَاداً وَثَمُودَاْ}: accusative by an implied «أَهْلَكْنا» ("We destroyed"), or conjoined to the object of «فأَخَذْتُهم», or to the object of {فَتَنَّا} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 3] at the beginning of the sūra — this is the view of al-Kisāʾī, and there is great remoteness in it. The tanwīn of Thamūd and its absence have preceded in Hūd.
Ibn Waththāb read «وعادٍ وثمودٍ» in the genitive, conjoined to «مَدْيَنَ», conjoined merely for indication, even though it does not follow that «شعيباً» was sent to them both; and it is not so.
His saying: {وَقَد تَّبَيَّنَ لَكُم}, i.e. what befell them. Al-Aʿmash read «مساكنُهم» in the nominative as the agent, with «مِنْ» omitted.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {وَقَارُونَ}: conjoined to «عاداً وثمودَ», or to the object of «فَصَدَّهم», or by an implied "remember".

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {فَكُلاًّ}: accusative by «أَخَذْنا». «بذَنْبه», i.e. because of, or accompanied by, his sin.
His saying: «مَنْ أَغْرَقْناه»: its referent pronoun is omitted because of its resemblance to a verse-ending. [Translator's note: the verse reads «مَنْ أَغْرَقْنا»; the source cites it with the pronoun.]

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {العنكبوت}: well known. Its nūn is radical, and the wāw and the tāʾ are additional, as proved by their saying in the plural عناكِب and in the diminutive عُنَيْكِب. It is treated as masculine and feminine; of the feminine is His saying «اتَّخَذَتْ», and of the masculine his saying:
3640 - على هَطَّالِهم منهمْ بيوتٌ ... كأنَّ العنكبوتَ هو ابْتَناها
(On their [mount] Haṭṭāl they have houses, as though the spider [masc.] had built them.)
This is regular in generic nouns: they are treated as masculine and feminine.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: its answer is omitted, i.e. "they would not have taken [as patrons] one for whom these parables are struck because of his insignificance". The object of the knowing cannot be of the type of His saying {وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ البيوت}, because everyone knows that; rather its object is implied, of the type the context indicates, i.e. "if they knew that this is their parable".

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {مَا يَدْعُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read it with the yāʾ of the third person, and the rest in the second person. «ما» may be a relative, accusative by «يَعْلَم», i.e. "He knows those whom they call upon, and knows their states", with «منْ شيء» a maṣdar. It may be interrogative, in which case two views are possible: that it, together with what governs it, is parenthetical between His saying «يَعْلَمُ» and His saying {وَهُوَ العزيز الحكيم}, as though it were said "what thing do they call upon besides Him?"; and the second: that it suspends (muʿalliqa) «يَعْلَم», so it is in the position of an accusative by it — al-Fārisī went to this. It may be negating, with «مِنْ» in «من شيء» redundant in the direct object, as though it were said: "they do not call upon besides Him anything that deserves to be called a thing"; the view in it then is that the clause is parenthetical, like the first of the two views of the interrogative. And it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival); Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "and شيء is a maṣdar". There is room for consideration in this, since the implied form would become "and He knows your calling upon anything of calling".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {نَضْرِبُهَا}: it may be the khabar (predicate) of «تلك», with «الأمثالُ» a naʿt (adjective), badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); or «الأمثالُ» may be the khabar and «نَضْرِبُها» a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may be a second khabar.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ الذين ظَلَمُواْ}: a conjoined exception (muttaṣil). There are two meanings in it. The first: except the wrongdoers — do not dispute with them at all, but contend with them by the sword. The second: dispute with them in a way other than the best, i.e. be harsh with them as they were harsh with you. Ibn ʿAbbās read «ألا», a particle of alerting, i.e. "so dispute with them".

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {مِن كِتَابٍ}: the object of «تَتْلُو», with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida). «مِنْ قبلِه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «كتاب», or attached to «تَتْلو» itself.
His saying: «إذاً لارتابَ»: an answer and a requital, i.e. had you recited a book before the Qurʾān, or been one who writes, the falsifiers would have doubted.

semin-durr:49-49.t: His saying: {بَلْ هُوَ آيَاتٌ}: Qatāda read «آيةٌ» in the singular.

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {آيَاتٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr read «آيةٌ» in the singular, because most of what comes in the Qurʾān is so. The rest [read] «آياتٌ» in the plural, because after it comes {قُلْ إِنَّمَا الآيات} in the plural by consensus, and the script admits it.

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying: {أَنَّآ أَنزَلْنَا}: the fāʿil (agent) of «يَكْفِهم».

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {وَيِقُولُ}: the Kufans and Nāfiʿ read it with the yāʾ of the third person, i.e. Allah the Exalted or the angel. The rest of the Seven [read it] with the nūn of majesty, for Allah the Exalted, or for the company of angels.
Abū al-Barahsam [read it] with the upper-dotted tāʾ, i.e. Hell, as in His saying {وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ} [Qāf: 30]. ʿAbdallāh and Ibn Abī ʿAbla [read] «ويُقال» in the passive.

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {فاعبدون}: al-Zamakhsharī made it the answer of an implied condition, and made the fronting of the object a compensation for its omission, while also conveying restriction. The Shaykh's dispute with him over its parallel has preceded.

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ}: Abū Bakr read it in the third person, and likewise in al-Rūm in His saying {ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ} [al-Rūm: 11]; Abū ʿAmr agreed with him in al-Rūm only. The rest [read] in the second person in both. It was also read «يَرْجِعُون» in the active voice.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: the two well-known views are possible in it: the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ishtighāl (occupation). The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read [لَنُثْوِيَنَّهم] with a three-dotted thāʾ with sukūn after the nūn and a yāʾ with fatḥa after the wāw, from الثَّواء, which is residing. The rest [read لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم] with a one-dotted bāʾ with fatḥa after the nūn and a hamza with fatḥa after the wāw, from المَباءة, which is lodging. [Translator's note: in both cases the source's "after the wāw" refers to the doubled/second radical position as written; translated as written.] On the first reading, «غُرفاً» is either a direct object by making «أَثْوَى» contain the meaning of «أنزل», so it is transitive to two objects — because ثوى is intransitive and the hamza gave it transitivity to one — or by likening the specific adverbial of place to the vague one, as in His saying {لأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَاطَكَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 16], or by dropping the preposition by latitude, i.e. "in chambers".
As for the second reading, it is a second object, because «بَوَّأ» is transitive to two objects; the Exalted said {تُبَوِّىءُ المؤمنين مَقَاعِدَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 121]; and it is also made transitive with the lām; the Exalted said {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لإِبْرَاهِيمَ} [al-Ḥajj: 26]. It was also read «لَنُثَوِّيَنَّهم», doubled, with the three-dotted thāʾ, made transitive by doubling just as it was made transitive by the hamza. And «تَجْرِي» is an adjective of «غُرَفاً».

semin-durr:59-59.t: His saying: {الذين صَبَرُواْ}: the genitive, the accusative and the nominative are possible in it, like its parallels that have preceded.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ}: Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted two views in «كَأَيِّن». The first: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «لا تحملُ» its adjective, «اللَّهُ يَرْزُقها» its khabar (predicate), and «مِنْ دابَّةٍ» an explication (tabyīn). The second: that it is in the position of an accusative by an implied verb explained by «يَرْزُقها», which is estimated after «كَأَيِّنْ» — meaning because it has the front position in speech. There is room for consideration in the second, because a condition of the explaining [verb] is that it be capable of governing, and this explaining [verb] does not govern, because if it governed it would take the place of the first, but it cannot take its place, since when the khabar is a verb that puts a singular pronoun in the nominative, its fronting before the mubtadaʾ is forbidden. If you want to know this rule, see Sūrat Hūd at His saying {أَلاَ يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفاً} [Hūd: 8].

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {الحيوان}: Abū al-Baqāʾ and others assumed a muḍāf before the mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the life of the Abode of the Hereafter". They only assumed that so that the mubtadaʾ and the khabar would correspond; hyperbole is better.
The wāw of «الحيوان» is from a yāʾ according to Sībawayh and his followers; it was only changed to a wāw irregularly, and likewise in «حَيْوَة» as a proper name. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Lest it be confused with the dual", meaning if one said حَيَيان. He said: "It was not changed to an alif, despite its having a vowel and what precedes it having a fatḥa, lest one of the two alifs be deleted." Others than Sībawayh took that at face value, so for them the final radical of الحياة is a wāw. Sībawayh has no proof in «حَيِي», because whenever what precedes a wāw has a kasra it is changed to a yāʾ, e.g. غُزِي, دُعِي and رَضِيَ.
His saying: {لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ}, i.e. had they known that it is the [true] life, they would not have preferred this world to it.

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what is His saying {فَإِذَا رَكِبُواْ فِي الفلك} connected? I say: to something omitted, indicated by what He described them with and set forth of their affair. Its meaning: they are as they were described, of associating partners and obstinacy; then when they embark…"

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {لِيَكْفُرُواْ}: it may be the lām of kay (purpose), which is the apparent view, or the lām of the imperative.
His saying: «ولِيَتَمَتَّعوا»: Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim and Warsh read it with kasra [on the lām], which admits the two preceding possibilities; the rest with sukūn, which is apparent in the imperative. If one holds the first lām to be for the imperative, he has conjoined an imperative to its like; if one holds it to be for causation, he has conjoined speech to speech.
ʿAbdallāh read {فَتَمَتَّعُواْ فَسَوْفَ تَعلَمُونَ}, and Abū al-ʿĀliya «فيُمَتَّعوا» with the lower-dotted yāʾ in the passive.

semin-durr:67-67.t: His saying: {أفبالباطل يُؤْمِنُونَ}: the generality read «يُؤْمنون» and «يكفرون» with the yāʾ of the third person; al-Ḥasan and al-Sulamī with the tāʾ of address in both.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying: {أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ}: an interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīr), as in his saying:
3641 - ألَسْتُمْ خيرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ المطايا ... وأندى العالمين بطونَ راحِ
(Are you not the best of those who ride mounts, and the most generous of all people in the palms of the hand?)
[Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as «364 - 1-», i.e. 3641.]

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {والذين جَاهَدُواْ}: what was possible in His saying {والذين آمَنُواْ} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 7] at the beginning of the sūra is possible in it. In it is a refutation of Thaʿlab, since he claimed that an oath clause does not occur as the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject).
His saying: «لَمع المحسنين»: of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to show their nobility.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا أَنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لَا يُفْتَنُونَ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا): أَنْ and what it governs take the place of the two objects.
(أَنْ يَقُولُوا): i.e. "for saying", or "because they say."
It may also be a badal (substitute) from «أَنْ يُتْرَكُوا». If the bāʾ is implied, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: the source has «الْيَاءُ» (the yāʾ), apparently a slip for «الْبَاءُ» (the bāʾ)]; and it may be implied with this meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئَاتِ أَنْ يَسْبِقُونَا سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَاءَ): it may operate as بِئْسَ operates; this has been mentioned at His saying: (بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا).
It may also have the meaning of قَبُحَ ("is evil"), in which case «مَا» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), or has the meaning of الذي, or is an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], and it is the fāʿil (agent) of سَاءَ.

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ لَآتٍ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو): «مَنْ» is conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb) is «فَإِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ»; the implied form is "will surely come to him."

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا وَإِنْ جَاهَدَاكَ لِتُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حُسْنًا): accusative by وَصَّيْنَا. It is also said: it is construed according to the meaning, the implied form being "We obligated him to goodness." It is also said: the implied form is likewise "possessed of goodness", as in His saying: (وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا).
It is also said: the meaning of وَصَّيْنَا is "We said to him: do good, a doing of good"; so it occupies the place of the maṣdar (verbal noun), or is a maṣdar with its augment letters dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ فِي الصَّالِحِينَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَنُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
«الَّذِينَ» may also be in the position of the accusative on the implied form "We will surely admit those who believed."

ukberi-tibyan:12-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنَا وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطَايَاكُمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِحَامِلِينَ مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ إِنَّهُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ (١٢) وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ وَأَثْقَالًا مَعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ وَلَيُسْأَلُنَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ (١٣) وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا فَأَخَذَهُمُ الطُّوفَانُ وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (١٤) فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَأَصْحَابَ السَّفِينَةِ وَجَعَلْنَاهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ (١٥) وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلْنَحْمِلْ خَطَايَاكُمْ): this is the lām of command; it is as though they commanded themselves. He turned to this from the declarative only because of the emphasis on commitment that it contains, as in the form of wonder (al-taʿajjub).
(مِنْ شَيْءٍ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and it is the object of the active participle.
(مِنْ خَطَايَاهُمْ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from شَيْءٍ; the implied form is "carrying anything of their sins."
(أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ): an adverb (ẓarf). The pronoun in «جَعَلْنَاهَا» refers to the punishment, or to the flood-event, or something similar.
(وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the object in «أَنْجَيْنَاهُ», or [accusative] on the implied form "and remember", or [conjoined] to أَرْسَلْنَا.

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ اللَّهُ يُنْشِئُ النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (النَّشْأَةَ الْآخِرَةَ): with the short form and with the long form [النَّشَاءَة] — two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ): the implied form is "nor whoever is in the heaven [able to escape] in it"; so مَن is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to أَنْتُمْ, and it is an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows].
It is also said: there is no omission in it, because «أَنْتُمْ» is an address to all, so the angels are included among them; then He specified after the general statement.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالَ إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَانًا مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ وَيَلْعَنُ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا وَمَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُمْ): concerning «مَا» there are three views. The first: it has the meaning of الذي, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "[which] you have taken"; «أَوْثَانًا» is a second object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); and «مَوَدَّةَ» is the khabar (predicate) according to the reading of whoever puts it in the nominative, the implied form being "possessors of affection." The second: it is the restraining [mā] (kāffa); أَوْثَانًا is an object; and مودّة in the accusative is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and in the nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause being a naʿt (adjective) of أوثان. The accusative may also be as an adjective, i.e. "possessors of affection." The third view: that «مَا» is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and «مَوَدَّةَ» in the nominative is the khabar. In this view there is no omission in the khabar, but rather in the noun of «إِنَّ», the implied form being "the cause of your taking [them] is affection."
«مَوَدَّةَ» is also read in genitive construct, both in the nominative and in the accusative.
And (بَيْنِكُمْ) in the genitive; and with tanwīn on مَوَدَّة in both ways [nominative and accusative], with بَيْنَ in the accusative.
Concerning what «فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا» is attached to, there are seven views:
The first: that it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتَّخَذْتُمْ if you make «مَا» restraining (kāffa), but not on the other two views, so as not to lead to separating the relative and what is in the ṣila (relative clause) by the khabar. The second: that it is attached to مودّة itself, if you do not make «بَيْنَ» an adjective of it, because a maṣdar does not govern when it is qualified. The third: that you attach it to «بَيْنِكُمْ» itself, because its meaning is "your coming together" or "your connection." The fourth: that you make it a second adjective of مودّة, if you give it tanwīn and make «بَيْنَكُمْ» an adjective. The fifth: that you attach it to مودّة and make «بَيْنَكُمْ» an adverb of place, so that «مَوَدَّةَ» governs both of them. The sixth: that you make it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «بَيْنِكُمْ», if you make it a description of مودّة. The seventh: that you make it a ḥāl from «بَيْنِكُمْ», since it is made definite by the genitive construct.
Some of them allowed «فِي» to be attached to مودّة even if «بَيْنِكُمْ» is an adjective, because there is latitude with adverbials, unlike the direct object.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلُوطًا إِذْ قَالَ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّكُمْ لَتَأْتُونَ الْفَاحِشَةَ مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلُوطًا): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نُوح; it has been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:33-40.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَمَّا أَنْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُنَا لُوطًا سِيءَ بِهِمْ وَضَاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا وَقَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ كَانَتْ مِنَ الْغَابِرِينَ (٣٣) إِنَّا مُنْزِلُونَ عَلَى أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ رِجْزًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ (٣٤) وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْنَا مِنْهَا آيَةً بَيِّنَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٣٥) وَإِلَى مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْبًا فَقَالَ يَاقَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَارْجُوا الْيَوْمَ الْآخِرَ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ (٣٦) فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ فَأَصْبَحُوا فِي دَارِهِمْ جَاثِمِينَ (٣٧) وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَ وَقَدْ تَبَيَّنَ لَكُمْ مِنْ مَسَاكِنِهِمْ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ السَّبِيلِ وَكَانُوا مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ (٣٨) وَقَارُونَ وَفِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ مُوسَى بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا كَانُوا سَابِقِينَ (٣٩) فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنْبِهِ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِ حَاصِبًا وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَخَذَتْهُ الصَّيْحَةُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ خَسَفْنَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ أَغْرَقْنَا وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَظْلِمَهُمْ وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ (٤٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ): the kāf is in the position of the genitive according to Sībawayh; on this view «أَهْلَكَ» is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We will save your family." According to al-Akhfash, it is in the position of the accusative or the genitive, and its position is accusative, so [أهلك] is conjoined to the position, because the genitive construct here is in the sense of separation, just as if the muḍāf ilayhi were an overt noun. Sībawayh distinguishes between the pronoun and the overt noun, saying that it is not permissible to retain the nūn of the dual and the plural with a pronoun, just as with tanwīn, whereas all of that is permissible with an overt noun.
The pronoun in «مِنْهَا» refers to the punishment.
(شُعَيْبًا): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نُوح; and the fāʾ in «فَقَالَ» conjoins to the implied أَرْسَلْنَا.
(عَادًا وَثَمُودَ): i.e. "and remember", or "and We destroyed."
(وَقَارُونَ) and what follows it likewise; it may also be maʿṭūf to the hāʾ in «صَدِّهِمْ» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has فَصَدَّهُمْ].
(كُلًّا): accusative by «أَخَذْنَا». «مَنْ» in «مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا» and what follows it is an indefinite noun qualified [by what follows], and some of the returning pronouns are omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا وَإِنَّ أَوْهَنَ الْبُيُوتِ لَبَيْتُ الْعَنْكَبُوتِ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ (٤١)).
The nūn in عَنْكَبُوت (spider) is radical, and the tāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), because of their saying, in its plural, عَنَاكِب.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَا إِلَّا الْعَالِمُونَ (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا يَدْعُونَ): it is an interrogative in the position of the accusative by «يَدْعُونَ», not by «يَعْلَمُ», and «مِنْ شَيْءٍ» is a clarification (tabyīn). It is also said: «مَا» has the meaning of الذي.
It may also be maṣdariyya (infinitival), and «شَيْءٍ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it may be negative, with «مِنْ» redundant (zāʾida), شَيْئًا being the object of «يَدْعُونَ».
(نَضْرِبُهَا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأمثال. It may also be a khabar (predicate), with «الْأَمْثَالُ» a naʿt (adjective).

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تُجَادِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْهُمْ وَقُولُوا آمَنَّا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَإِلَهُنَا وَإِلَهُكُمْ وَاحِدٌ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا): it is an exception from the same genus (istithnāʾ min al-jins), and concerning the meaning there are two views.
The first: "except those who do wrong — do not dispute with them in the best way, but rather with harshness, because they are harsh with you"; so it is excepted from «الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ», not from the disputing. The second: "do not dispute with them at all, but let the sword judge them, because of the excess of their obstinacy."

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ يُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَرَحْمَةً وَذِكْرَى لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا): it is the fāʿil (agent) of يَكْفِهِمْ.

ukberi-tibyan:58-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا نِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ (٥٨) الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
It may also be in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by the verb mentioned.
(غُرَفًا): a second object; its parallel has been mentioned in Yūnus and al-Ḥajj.
(الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ لَا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمْ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ): it may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), «مِنْ دَابَّةٍ» being a clarification (tabyīn).
(لَا تَحْمِلُ): a naʿt (adjective) of دَابَّة.
(اللَّهُ يَرْزُقُهَا): a clause that is the khabar (predicate) of كَأَيِّنْ; the pronoun is made feminine according to the meaning.
It may also be in the position of the accusative by a verb indicated by يَرْزُقُهَا, implied after كَأَيِّنْ.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ الْحَيَوَانُ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنَّ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ): i.e. "the life of the abode", because He predicated الحيوان of it, and that is life. The final radical (lām) of الحَيَوَان is yāʾ; the origin is حَيَيَان, and the yāʾ was changed to wāw so that it would not be confused with the dual; and it was not changed to alif, despite its being vowelled and preceded by fatḥa, so that one of the two alifs would not be dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا): whoever gives the lām kasra makes it have the meaning of كَيْ (so that); whoever gives it sukūn, it may be likewise, and it may be a command. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَعادًا وثَمُودَ وقَدْ تَبَيَّنَ لَكم مِن مَساكِنِهِمْ﴾ — the meaning is: "And We destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd", because before this come Qārūn and his companions, ﴿فَأخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ﴾ (so the earthquake seized them). [Translator's note: the source says Qārūn and his companions come before this; in the muṣḥaf the preceding verses (36–37) concern Madyan and Shuʿayb, and Qārūn is mentioned in verse 39 after it. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿فَكُلا أخَذْنا بِذَنْبِهِ فَمِنهم مَن أرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِ حاصِبًا﴾ — these are the people of Lūṭ; ﴿وَمِنهم مَن أخَذَتْهُ الصَّيْحَةُ﴾ — these are the people of Thamūd, and Madyan; ﴿وَمِنهم مَن خَسَفْنا بِهِ الأرْضَ﴾ — these are Qārūn and his companions; ﴿وَمِنهم مَن أغْرَقْنا﴾ — these are the people of Nūḥ, and Pharaoh. So Allah made known that what was done to them was justice, that He did not wrong them, and that they wronged themselves, because He had made things clear to them; and that is His saying: ﴿وَكانُوا مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 38] — they did what they did although He had made clear to them that its outcome would be their punishment.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أوْلِياءَ كَمَثَلِ العَنْكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا﴾ — the verse. ”لَوْ“ is connected to His saying ”اِتَّخَذُوا“, i.e. "if they knew that their taking of protectors is like the spider's taking [of a house]"; it is not that they do not know that the spider's house is weak. That is because there is no house weaker than the spider's house among what vermin make for themselves as dwellings, nor any that gives less protection from heat or cold. The meaning is that their protectors do not diminish them [Translator's note: so in the source, «لا يَنْقُصُونَهُمْ»; probably a copyist's error for «لا يَنْفَعُونَهُمْ», "do not benefit them"], do not provide for them, and do not ward off any harm from them, just as the spider's house does not protect the spider.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأقِمِ الصَّلاةَ إنَّ الصَّلاةَ تَنْهى عَنِ الفَحْشاءِ والمُنْكَرِ﴾ — al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: "Whoever is not restrained by his prayer from indecency and wrongdoing, his prayer is no prayer, and it is a burden of ruin upon him."
His saying: ﴿وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ﴾ — there are several aspects (awjuh) in it. Among them: that ”أكْبَرُ“ is in the meaning of ”كَبِيرٌ“ (great). And it has come in the tafsīr: "Allah's remembrance of you when you remember Him is greater than your remembrance [of Him]." Another aspect, whose meaning is: ”وَلَذِكْرُ اللَّهِ أكْبَرُ“ — it, the prohibition of indecency and wrongdoing, is greater than refraining from indecency and wrongdoing, because Allah has forbidden them both.

zajjaj:46-46.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُجادِلُوا أهْلَ الكِتابِ إلا بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾ — i.e. the people of war [Translator's note: so in the source, «أهْلَ الحَرْبِ»; the explanation that follows speaks of the people of the jizya, and the intended sense may be "not the people of war"]. So the meaning is: "Do not dispute with the people of the jizya (poll-tax) except in the way that is best, and fight those who have done wrong." And it has been said: the verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿قاتِلُوا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ ولا بِاليَوْمِ الآخِرِ ولا يُحَرِّمُونَ ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ ورَسُولُهُ ولا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ الحَقِّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ حَتّى يُعْطُوا الجِزْيَةَ عَنْ يَدٍ وهم صاغِرُونَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 29]; so the state of being humbled (al-ṣaghār) lay outside "اَلَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ" (the way that is best), and therefore it is more likely that it is abrogated. It is also possible that the humbling is the taking of the jizya from them even if they dislike it. Those from whom the jizya is taken — by the explicit text of the Book — are the Jews and the Christians, because they are the people of the Torah and the Gospel. As for the Magians, the jizya was taken from them because of the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «سُنُّوا بِهِمْ سُنَّةَ أهْلِ الكِتابِ» ("Treat them in the way the People of the Book are treated"). People have differed about the other unbelievers besides these, such as idol-worshippers and those like them. According to Mālik ibn Anas they are treated in the same way: the jizya is taken from them, whether they are non-Arabs or Arabs. As for the people of Iraq, they said: we accept the jizya from non-Arabs who are not Arabs, if they are unbelievers, even if they fall outside these categories — I mean the Jews, the Christians and the Magians — such as the Indians, the Turks and the Daylam. As for the Arabs, in their view, if they fall outside these three categories no jizya is accepted from them, and killing was the ruling in their case if they persisted in a religion other than Judaism, Christianity and Magianism. And some of the jurists hold nothing but killing for the worshippers of idols and statues and those like them.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما كُنْتَ تَتْلُو مِن قَبْلِهِ مِن كِتابٍ ولا تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ إذًا لارْتابَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ — i.e. you had not read the scriptures, nor were you one who writes; and such is the description of the Prophet ﷺ with them in the Torah and the Gospel.
His saying: ﴿إذًا لارْتابَ المُبْطِلُونَ﴾ — it has been said: they are the unbelievers of Quraysh.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ في صُدُورِ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ﴾ — it has been said that there are three aspects in it. Among them: "Rather, the Qur'an is clear signs." Among them: "Rather, the Prophet ﷺ and his affairs are clear signs." And among them: ”بَلْ هو آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ“, i.e. rather, [the fact] that he neither reads nor writes is clear signs; because if he had not read a book, nor was he one who writes, and then he told the stories of the ancients and of the prophets, then that is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge.

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَكْفِهِمْ أنّا أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الكِتابَ يُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — «Some people among the Muslims had written something down from the Jews, and they brought it to the Prophet ﷺ, and he, upon him be peace, said: "It is enough as foolishness of a people — or the misguidance of a people — that they turn away from what their prophet brought to what someone other than their prophet brought to a people other than theirs."»

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالعَذابِ ولَوْلا أجَلٌ مُسَمًّى لَجاءَهُمُ العَذابُ﴾ — this was revealed about an ignorant people who said: ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كانَ هَذا هو الحَقَّ مِن عِنْدِكَ فَأمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that there is a set term for their punishment, and He said: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهم والسّاعَةُ أدْهى وأمَرُّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46].
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهم بَغْتَةً﴾ — its meaning is: suddenly (fujāʾatan). ”بَغْتَةً“ is an accusative (manṣūb) noun in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its meaning is: "and it will surely come upon them taking them by surprise (mufājaʾatan)."

zajjaj:56-56.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّ أرْضِي واسِعَةٌ فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — its interpretation: it has been said that they were commanded to emigrate from the place in which they could not worship Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and fulfil His obligations. The origin of this concerns those who were able [to emigrate] among those who believed and could not make their faith manifest. And likewise it is obligatory upon everyone who is in a land in which disobedience is practised, and who cannot do otherwise, to emigrate and move to where it is possible for him to worship Allah as He truly deserves to be worshipped.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — ”إيّايَ“ is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb, which the one that appears explains. The meaning is: "So worship Me — so worship Me" (”فاعْبُدُوا إيّايَ فاعْبُدُونِي“); so one of the two verbs — I mean the second — dispensed with making the first overt. If you say ”فَإيّايَ فاعْبُدُوا“, then ”إيّايَ“ is accusative by what comes after the fā', and you do not make it accusative by an implied verb, just as when you say ”بِزَيْدٍ فامْرُرْ“ (by Zayd, pass), the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ”اُمْرُرْ“. The meaning is: "My earth is spacious, so worship Me." As for the fā' when you say ”زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْ“ (Zayd, strike), it can only be an apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, as if someone said: "I do not strike ʿAmr, but I strike Zayd," and you said in answer to him: "Then strike Zayd," and then you said: ”زَيْدًا فاضْرِبْ“, making the fronting of the noun a substitute for the condition, as if you had said: "If the matter is as you describe, then strike Zayd." And this is the position of all the Basran grammarians.

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم مِنَ الجَنَّةِ غُرَفًا﴾ — and it has been read ”لَنُثَوِّيَنَّهم“, with thāʾ. One says ”ثَوى الرَّجُلُ“ (the man dwelt) when he stays in a place, and ”أثْوَيْتُهُ“ (I lodged him): I settled him in a dwelling in which he stays.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن دابَّةٍ لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَها﴾ — every living creature on the earth, of what has reason and what has no reason, is a dābba (creature); it is simply from ”دَبَّتْ عَلى الأرْضِ، فَهي دابَّةٌ“ (it crept on the earth, so it is a creeper). The meaning is: "a creeping soul (nafs dābba)." And the meaning of ”وَكَأيِّنْ“ is: "and how many a creature (وَكَمْ مِن دابَّةٍ)."
His saying: ﴿لا تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَها﴾ — i.e. it does not store up its provision; it simply wakes in the morning and Allah provides for it. Most animals and creeping things are like this, and among the animals that creep there is none that stores up, as far as has become clear, except the ant, for its storing is evident.

zajjaj:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ الدّارَ الآخِرَةَ لَهي الحَيَوانُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — its meaning: it is the abode of everlasting life.

zajjaj:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا رَكِبُوا في الفُلْكِ دَعَوُا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ — i.e. they did not pray that their idols, and what they worship alongside Allah, would save them; ﴿فَلَمّا نَجّاهم إلى البَرِّ إذا هم يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ — i.e. they worship others alongside Allah.

zajjaj:66-66.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ — it has been read with kasra on the lām and with sukūn on it, and the kasra is better, in the sense of: "so that they disbelieve, and so that they enjoy themselves."

zajjaj:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهم سُبُلَنا﴾ — Allah made known that He increases those who strive in guidance; just as He leads the transgressors astray and increases the unbelievers in misguidance through their unbelief, so He increases those who strive in guidance. Thus He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿والَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا زادَهم هُدًى وآتاهم تَقْواهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 17]; the meaning is that He gave them the reward of their piety and increased them in guidance upon their guidance.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ — its interpretation: Allah is their helper, because His saying ﴿والَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا فِينا﴾ — Allah being with them — indicates His helping them; and help consists in their rising above their enemy by prevailing through proof, and prevailing through force and power.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿أحَسِبَ النّاسُ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 2]: "الـم" — its interpretation is: "I am Allah, I know best (أنا اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ)". We have explained everything that has been said about this at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿أحَسِبَ النّاسُ أنْ يُتْرَكُوا أنْ يَقُولُوا آمَنّا﴾: the wording is the wording of an inquiry, and the meaning is the meaning of affirmation and rebuke (taqrīr wa-tawbīkh). Its meaning is: "Did they think that We would be satisfied from them with their saying 'we are believers', only, and that they would not be tested with what makes clear the reality of their faith?" It has come in the exegesis concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَهم لا يُفْتَنُونَ﴾: "they will not be tested with that by which the truthfulness of their faith is known from its falsity"; and it was said: "لا يُفْتَنُونَ" means: they will not be tried in their persons and their wealth, so that through patience under trial the one true in faith is known from others. The position of the first "أنْ" is accusative, [standing for] the ism (noun) of "حَسِبَ" and its khabar (predicate). The position of the second "أنْ" is accusative from two angles. The better of them is that it be accusative through "يُتْرَكُوا", so the meaning is: "Did people think that they would be left for saying (لِأنْ يَقُولُوا)" or "because of saying (بِأنْ يَقُولُوا)"; when the genitive particle was dropped, "يُتْرَكُوا" reached "أنْ" and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition). It is also possible that what governs the second is "أحَسِبَ"; as though the meaning on this view — and Allah knows best — were: "Did people think that they would say 'we believe' and not be tested?" The first is better.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنّا الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾, i.e. We tested and tried.
And His saying: ﴿فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا ولَيَعْلَمَنَّ الكاذِبِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "He will surely know the truthfulness of the truthful through his truthfulness actually occurring from him, and the lying of the liar through his lying actually occurring from him; and that is what is recompensed." Allah knew the truthful from the liar before He created them both; but the intent is the knowledge's coming to pass of that which is recompensed.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿أمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ السَّيِّئاتِ أنْ يَسْبِقُونا﴾, i.e. they think that they will escape Us, i.e. they cannot frustrate Us. ﴿ساءَ ما يَحْكُمُونَ﴾, with the meaning "evil is it as a judgement that they judge (ساءَ حُكْمًا يَحْكُمُونَ)", just as you say: "an excellent man is Zayd (نِعْمَ رَجُلًا زَيْدٌ)". It is also possible that it [ما] is nominative, with the meaning: "evil is the judgement, their judgement (ساءَ الحُكْمُ حُكْمُهم)".

zajjaj:5-5.t:
And His saying: ﴿مَن كانَ يَرْجُو لِقاءَ اللَّهِ﴾: its meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "whoever hopes for the reward of meeting Allah". As for whoever said that its meaning is fear: fear is the opposite of hope, and there is no [word with] opposite [meanings] in the speech; we have explained that in the Book of Opposites (Kitāb al-Aḍdād).
And His saying: ﴿فَإنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾: "مَن" is in the sense of a condition; it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "كانَ", and the apodosis (jawāb al-jazāʾ) is: ﴿فَإنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ لآتٍ﴾.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾: the reading is "حُسْنًا", and "إحْسانًا" has also been transmitted. "حُسْنًا" is better because it agrees with the Muṣḥaf. Whoever says "حُسْنًا", it is like "We enjoined (وَصَّيْنا)" [him] to do toward his parents what is good. Whoever reads "إحْسانًا", its meaning is: "We enjoined man to do good to his parents, a doing of good (أنْ يُحْسِنَ إلى والِدَيْهِ إحْسانًا)".
